It reads saved checkpoints, so unlike autocode --run-dir RUN --status it inspects no supervised process: a row says what the run last saved, not whether its provider is still alive. registry list is the pointer index with each pointer's availability; runs is what each run now wants from you. autocode events [--run-dir RUN] [--follow] One saved run's recorded events as a JSON-lines stream: how it got to where --status says it stands, one event per line, printed exactly as the run wrote it. These are the run's own records — its approvals, answers, contract and configuration changes, routing decisions and self-taken recoveries — not a provider's transcript. --follow keeps printing new events until the run ends the stream, and the status view contract is what ends it: a completed run exits 0, a run that needs a person exits 2 after naming that person's command on stderr, and --timeout SECONDS bounds the wait. Stdout is always JSON lines, so --json does not apply; the envelope is run-event.schema.json, whose kind is an open vocabulary a consumer must tolerate. Read-only, and like runs it inspects no supervised process: a stage hung mid-flight keeps the stream open, so ask autocode --run-dir RUN --status whether it is alive. autocode plan --export PATH [--run-dir RUN] [--json] / autocode plan --check PATH [--json] / autocode plan --render PATH [--json] Write a saved run's current plan (shown for approval or approved) as a Markdown file to review in a pull request: a front matter holding the contract body exactly, its goal hash (the SHA-256 of the body) and the revision it came from, then the plan as text generated from it. Never the approval token; credential-shaped text is masked as in bundle, and the export then says the file's goal hash differs from the run's. --check reads such a file and prints its goal hash, and exits 2 when the file cannot be read or its text no longer matches its front matter. --render regenerates that text after the front matter was edited. Reads the checkpoint like events: no run lock, nothing recorded, nothing launched; only the named file is written. --json formats results or error endings as structured JSON. See Reviewing a plan in a pull request. autocode wait [--run-dir RUN] [--timeout S] The blocking form of autocode runs: wait on one saved run until it reaches you, ends, or stops advancing on its own. Each second it rereads the checkpoint and, read-only, inspects whether a controller still owns the run — the one question a saved status cannot answer. The outcome names which ended the wait: complete (the run reported TASK_COMPLETE/COMPLETE; exit 0), needs_you (the status view names what you must do, and the command that answers it; exit 2), controller_lost (the saved status is still RUNNING but nothing owns the run, so it will not advance on its own; exit 2, pointing at --status), stopped (anything else; exit 2), or timeout when --timeout SECONDS elapses first (exit 2, reporting the last observed status and controller). --json prints the outcome as exactly one JSON object. Nothing here starts, resumes or changes a run. autocode intervention submit\|inspect Queued interventions (see Interventions).

When working on AutoCode itself, the launcher on PATH may use an older installed package. Run autocode doctor --workspace /path/to/autocode --json to compare its application payload with a verified AutoCode checkout. The install-drift warning names the executing path, the checkout commit and changed, missing or extra package files. Matching payloads do not warn even when an installed build's commit is unknown. Customer repositories are never treated as AutoCode provenance.

To run the checkout directly from its root, use python tools/autocode.py doctor (or python tools/autocode.py with your ordinary task options). Doctor also prints a deliberately invoked reinstall command for the current interpreter. It never updates an installation or rewrites run state itself.

The old console-script aliases remain for compatibility. The unit entry points autopilot, autoplanner, autocode-build, autoreview, autoresolver, autocode-orchestrator and autocode-unattended are internal entry points; use autocode and its public subcommands in new instructions. Internal stage and unit names keep their existing meaning.

docs.title: Offline demo
docs.text:
Run autocode demo after installation; Git and Python are enough. You do not need OpenCode, Codex or an account. The demo answers its sample requirements question and approves its displayed sample plan, then runs real CLI checks. It first shows a claimed passing check that AutoCode refuses when its independent rerun fails. The successful sample also stops at the completion gate until demo acceptance of the artifact is recorded. These automatic approvals apply only to the new demo project.

The command prints the run directory, canonical evidence record and demo.json, and keeps every output inside its new directory. To choose where it goes, use autocode demo --directory /path/to/new-demo; the directory must not exist. Remove that directory after inspection. Fake-provider evidence demonstrates the workflow and is separate from the real-model reliability results.

docs.title: Supplying a brief
docs.text:
Flag Meaning --brief TEXT Start a new run with literal task text; --brief - reads UTF-8 bytes from stdin. Mutually exclusive with a positional task, --brief-file, saved-run options and resume. --brief-file PATH Start a new run with the file's exact UTF-8 task text, retaining line breaks and trailing whitespace. Mutually exclusive with a positional task, --brief, saved-run options and resume.

Use autocode --brief-file brief.txt or pipe UTF-8 text into autocode --brief - to preserve backticks, $(), quotes and line breaks exactly. These inputs start a new run and cannot accompany a positional task, resume or --run-dir. An empty or invalid UTF-8 input is refused before creating a run.

--brief TEXT and the positional task remain available. The shell processes arguments before AutoCode receives them: use single quotes around literal shell syntax, for example autocode 'Fix the `run()` function', or use a file or stdin when the brief contains embedded single quotes. AutoCode cannot recover text already changed by the caller's shell. The saved task and its UTF-8 SHA-256 appear as view.task and view.task_sha256 in status JSON; compare them with the source brief before continuing.

docs.title: Targeting a run
docs.text: Flag Meaning --workspace /path Committed Git workspace to work in. Defaults to the current directory. Without a task or --run-dir, where AutoCode looks for the run to act on. --run-dir /path Act on this saved run, from any directory. Without --workspace, the run's own checkout is used. --in-place Start a new task in the selected checkout instead of a fresh worktree. Uncommitted and untracked files there count as the code the task starts from (see Workflow). Only one run's agents work in a checkout at a time; a second run exits with status 2 and changes nothing (see Task lanes). --workflow build\|bugfix\|review\|design\|discuss Name the kind of job instead of having Requirements (or, on a flow without it, the recognizer) name it from the request. A pinned build still runs Requirements first; any other kind starts its own first stage. Also accepted by a saved run whose job is not named yet. A run whose job is already decided keeps it: start a new run to change it (see Workflow). --status Read-only status, including milestone_checkpoint, interventions, active_stage.activity. --json Stdout carries exactly one JSON object unless the invocation ends with an error message other than a refused setting (below); everything else the invocation prints goes to stderr. A finished or paused run prints the same payload --status prints. A user action (an approval, answer, feedback, resolver response and the like) prints that payload plus result: exit_code, saved, message (the text a person would have read) and error, which is {"code": "input_rejected", "message": …} when the input was refused and null otherwise. A refusal before the run loads prints {"result": …} alone. Any other invocation that loaded the run and returned without printing the payload, such as one stopped by --pause-after-stage or a time or iteration limit, prints the saved run's payload plus result. A setting the run's configuration refuses as the run loads still ends with autocode: … on stderr, and also prints the saved run's payload plus result ({"result": …} alone for a new run refused before its first checkpoint), whose error is input_rejected with the refusal text. Such settings include --single-model, --spec-first, --blind-tests, --utility-model, --builder-strong-model or a different --engine on a saved run, --single-model with a per-role model flag, --max-milestone-seconds on a saved run without milestone checkpoints, and the tool-containment refusals: --allow-uncontained-tools on a run with no built-in OpenCode stage, or a built-in OpenCode run without it where the kernel tool boundary is unavailable. The refused setting is not saved, though a new run without --in-place may already have created its task worktree and branch, which result.message names. In a native visual run (a task with a VISUAL_REVIEW_PROFILE= directive) such a refusal is instead saved as a PAUSED_INVALID_OUTPUT pause and printed like any other pause, with error null. Any other invocation that ends with an error message (autocode: … or argparse's usage: text on stderr) prints nothing on stdout. A refusal reported in result also prints {"error": …} on its own line of stderr: its last line, except after a refused setting, where autocode: … follows. status-view.schema.json describes the status payload. The lone {"result": …} does not validate against the schema's root; its result validates against the schema's properties.result. Exit codes are unchanged (Exit codes); a usage error still prints argparse's text. The read-only commands (--status, --explain, --dry-run, doctor --json, registry, usage --json) print their own output and are unaffected. --explain Read-only explanation of a saved run's stop and what the next command does. With an explicit task in a Git workspace, previews the initial explanation without creating a run. An explicit --run-dir cannot accompany a new task or new-run inputs. --dry-run Read-only preview; never emits an accepted handoff. --inspect-evidence With --status, inspect the current source and saved verification evidence without running checks. --summary With --status (or autocode status), print the run in one sentence instead of the JSON payload: Needs you, Working, Done or Stopped, then Next: and the exact command the status view names, when there is one. A run whose last controller exited on purpose after a saved answer, approval or follow-up (a ready controller receipt for the current checkpoint) reads Needs you: Saved and ready to continue; nothing runs it until you do. rather than Working. When the run waits on questions, the pending questions follow, each with its options and proposed default, as the readable tail of a full --status does before the Answer with: command. Done means completion is verified against the current checkout; a finished run without that, or a checkpoint that says running while nothing supervises it, reads Stopped. The same object is view.summary in the JSON payload; --status without --summary keeps every detail.

docs.title: Understanding a stop
docs.text:
The status view adds pause_category, its readable pause_category_label, and next_command. The category says whose action is needed; the exact status and stop_reason remain available as detail, together with the existing needs and recovery tokens.

Category Meaning your_decision — Your decision Inspect and answer a question, approve a plan, or authorize a recovery or limit change. your_environment — Your environment Repair the workspace, configuration, prerequisites or other local setup. model_or_provider — Model or provider Inspect a model refusal, quota stop, provider failure or incomplete model output. autocode — AutoCode Inspect an internal consistency, supervision or completion-proof stop.

Rejected human actions and invalid configuration changes also print the current recovery summary and command. Answer a clarification with --answer Q=TEXT and the displayed private resolver token; --resolver-response is for an operational request. A rejected response does not turn a clarification into an operational pause or grant a retry.

Use the offered next_command under the category. It is derived from the same current needs and actions as the existing recovery instructions; the category never approves, retries or changes a limit. next_command is null when the run has no executable next action. Resolve any stated prerequisite before running a command that resumes work. Replace ANSWER, MODEL, N or GOAL_FILE with your intended input; a displayed token uses its paired environment variable with the - selector. When recovery has two steps, next_command gives the first one; inspect status again after it. A missing issued token offers a noninteractive display, and a missing source identity offers inspection rather than an unbound retry. autocode explain describes the stop and the offered action. See the status view contract.

docs.title: Which run a command acts on
docs.text:
A command with no task and no --run-dir acts on a saved run found from the --workspace directory: the run directory you are in; otherwise the runs of the task worktree you are in; otherwise the project's in-place runs and the runs of all its task worktrees. It names the run on stderr (Using the saved run RUN (STATUS, ...)) and goes on as if you had passed --run-dir RUN.

Command Run it takes autocode, autocode resume, --resume-paused and its --retry-* companions, --unit The only unfinished run. A finished run (TASK_COMPLETE, or stopped) is never relaunched this way, and a run that autocode tasks drives is left to that command. --status, --explain, --dry-run, autocode status, autocode explain The only unfinished run; with none, the latest finished one. --show-goal, --answer, --approve-goal, --feedback and the other user actions The only unfinished run, preferring one no task flow drives. These save the run, so they never pick a finished one. --follow-up The most recently completed run, preferring one no task flow drives. Refused when a run started after it finished has not finished: name the run with --run-dir.

A new task (autocode "TEXT") always starts a new run. When an unfinished run of this project already carries exactly that text, the start first prints a note on stderr naming each such run and the autocode --run-dir RUN that continues it, so a recalled start command does not quietly leave two runs of one request behind (#2340).

docs.title: Keeping authorization tokens out of argv
docs.text:
These options accept - to read their paired environment variable:

Token option Environment variable --resolver-token AUTOCODE_RESOLVER_TOKEN --job-retry-token AUTOCODE_JOB_RETRY_TOKEN --recover-job-report AUTOCODE_RECOVER_JOB_REPORT --approve-goal AUTOCODE_APPROVE_GOAL_TOKEN --changeset-token AUTOCODE_CHANGESET_TOKEN --review-token AUTOCODE_REVIEW_TOKEN --expected-goal-token AUTOCODE_EXPECTED_GOAL_TOKEN --expected-recovery-token AUTOCODE_EXPECTED_RECOVERY_TOKEN checkpoint --expected-token AUTOCODE_CHECKPOINT_EXPECTED_TOKEN

Prefer this on shared machines: Linux exposes /proc/<pid>/cmdline to every local user, while /proc/<pid>/environ is readable only by the owner, and a typed token also lands in shell history. The environment variable alone never authorizes anything — the flag must still be present. TaskRun, dashboard actions and the trial driver pass these tokens through each CLI child's environment. Their process arguments and saved command records contain -. Literal CLI tokens remain supported. The controller always removes all eight variables before launching a provider or test command, even if named in AUTOCODE_PASS_ENV. Programmatic command builders require full token option names; abbreviated token options are refused before recording or launch.

With several unfinished runs the command changes nothing, exits 2 and lists them with the --run-dir command for each. With no run it says where it looked; with only finished runs, a bare autocode names the latest one instead of relaunching it. Inside a run directory whose state.json is missing or cannot be used, or one autocode clean-worktrees archived, it refuses rather than pick another run. A task, or a new-run option (--in-place, --figma-file, --figma-manifest, --figma-review, --ui-run, --builder-strong-model, --conversation-handoff, --test-root, --package), starts a new run instead; autocode resume never does.

docs.title: Conversation and approval
docs.text:
--status keeps its JSON document on stdout and prints a short pending-question list and the current Resolver token on stderr. After a successful --answer, stderr shows the questions still open and their new token, or says there are no questions left to answer. Use that new token for the next answer; answering does not approve a plan or start a model.

Flag Meaning --chat Interactive chat mode (default in a terminal). --no-chat One command per turn (default for non-interactive). --answer 'Q1=…' Answer a question the run is waiting on (repeatable; the status view's needs.kind is answer). Requires the current --resolver-token shown by Resolver. A finished run waits on none: the questions in its report take --follow-up (see Waiting or finished). --answer route-sol=MODEL At a quota stop (PAUSED_BUDGET), a content-filter refusal (PAUSED_CONTENT_FILTER), an authenticated output-limit stop (PAUSED_OUTPUT_CAP) or a context-window stop (PAUSED_CONTEXT_WINDOW: the request no longer fit, or the provider compacted the conversation), name the model the stopped role continues on. Requires the current --resolver-token. The model must suit the role's engine, be listed by OpenCode on OpenCode runs and keep the cross-model rule; otherwise the run stays paused with the question open. Sets the stopped attempt aside as --abandon-stage does and records a route_assignment; continue with --resume-paused. The resume-flag form is --abandon-stage ATTEMPT, then --resume-paused --sol-model MODEL. A stopped workflow job (needs.kind retry_job with needs.route) takes --answer route-ROLE=MODEL --job-retry-token TOKEN instead: no resolver token, no --abandon-stage, no --ROLE-model flag; it issues a new job retry token, so continue with --resume-paused --retry-failed-stage --job-retry-token NEW_TOKEN (Waiting or finished). See Models. --answer effort-ROLE=EFFORT At PAUSED_EFFORT_UNSUPPORTED, a reasoning effort you named that the role's model does not declare: name one of the variants the stop lists (the status view's needs.effort.declared). No attempt or issued token is involved, as for a cross-model stop. Saves the level as your own choice (origin user_explicit) and records an effort_assignment; the run waits at the same pause, and --resume-paused then continues. A variant the model does not declare is refused with nothing saved. See Reasoning effort. --feedback '…' Send a correction; returns to discovery and requires fresh approval. With --adaptive-planning, feedback on a plan shown for approval goes to the Planner, which revises it. Refused at an operational pause unless it offers feedback (an exhausted plan-review budget, a validation-only stop). --follow-up '…' Say the next thing to a finished run ("Fix them." after a review): the run starts at Requirements again, which names the new job, and continues in the same run directory. Finished runs only (TASK_COMPLETE); any other run exits 2 unchanged. After a design review, the reply revises that review: the Architect keeps every concern under its id, keeps a settled one as resolved with what settled it, and adds the revision to revisions in review/design-review.json (Replying to a design review). After a design turn, "Build it." builds that design as approved: it is checked against the code first (check_design). The message is saved as feedback that planning can cite for requested contract changes; the new plan still needs approval. --delegate Q1 Accept a question's proposed default. Requires the current --resolver-token shown by Resolver. --delegate-all --review-token 'r3:<hash>' Delegate every pending question marked delegable with a proposed default, on the exact displayed revision. Refuses the whole call if any question lacks a default, is not delegable, has a protected or missing category (cost, quota, permission, external side effect, requested outcome), or asks about a rejected assumption. Never approves; invalidates any existing approval. --reject-assumption A1 --review-token 'r3:<hash>' Reject a structured assumption from the displayed requirements handoff (repeatable). A stale token, or a handoff refreshed since display, is refused. Never approves; invalidates any existing approval. --show-goal Display the current contract/revision. At the approval stop it also says what approving authorizes and what the token locks, and ends with a summary of the decision (outcome, permissions, criteria and how each is checked, what passing proves), the limits in effect and the exact approve command (sample). --details At a plan approval stop, print the full brief (the contract, its diff from the last revision, file hashes and request tokens) instead of the short approval screen. Without it, the stop shows the decision first: what the plan will do, what it may change, the criteria and how each is checked, what passing proves, the limits, then the approve and change commands. In the terminal chat, /details does the same. --show-goal and --json are unchanged. --approve-goal 'r3:<hash>' Approve the exact displayed revision. --changeset-token TOKEN With --approve-goal on a saved run, bind the approval to a prepared change set. The coordinator supplies this through TaskRun; use changeset approve to review and approve all member plans. Builders remain held until every member has accepted the same set. --related-profile PATH Fresh runs only: inherit the coordinator's pinned role routes and limits. Requires its exact --related-profile-sha256; target approval policy remains enforced. The core supplies this for related runs. --related-profile-sha256 SHA256 Exact hash of --related-profile; both options are required together. --assign-linked-scope IDENTITY On a saved run, accept the core's exact repository assignment for the current scope identity. Requires the matching registered change set; grants no plan approval. --edit-goal body.json Load a full contract body as a new draft revision. Refused at an operational pause unless it offers feedback (an exhausted plan-review budget, a validation-only stop). --goal-file PATH Load a plan file (autocode plan --export, reviewed and edited in a pull request) into a saved run as its next draft revision, as --edit-goal loads a body; the plan then goes through ordinary approval (in joint planning the Plan Reviewer reviews it first). Refused with the run left as it was when the file cannot be read, its text no longer matches its front matter, it still holds text the export masked as credential-shaped, its runner records are not the run's, or a planner's draft of it would be sent back: a literal the request states that the plan drops (with the message the planner gets), a Go test the request names that no criterion proves by that name, git status in a check, or a command the shell cannot parse. The approval stop then names the file and its goal hash and says whether the plan to approve is still the plan loaded from it, and the completed run's evidence report (and the PR body built from it) cites the file, its goal hash and the approved plan's. Refused at an operational pause unless it offers feedback (an exhausted plan-review budget, a validation-only stop). It does not start a new run. See Reviewing a plan in a pull request. --approve-review C1 --review-token '…' Record a human-review decision for criterion C1. --as NAME With --approve-goal, --approve-review, --accept-completion, --edit-goal, --goal-file or a resume (--resume-paused, or autocode resume at a pause) on a shared machine: the name of the person approving, accepting completion, editing or resuming, saved beside the Git identity as their claim, never verified (Who approved). With a resume it is saved only when the resume releases a pause; a resume that finds none, or that the pause keeps, ignores it. --status, the completion summary and, for a build, bug-fix or design run, the completed run's evidence report (and so the autocode-issue pr body) list it with the rest of the record. A project's require-approver checks the Git identity, never this name (Required approver). --reject-review C1 --review-token '…' --review-note TEXT Reject the current reviewed artifact for criterion C1, retaining the nonempty note as feedback for a fresh plan and approval. Uses the same artifact freshness checks as approval. --investigator-model MODEL, --investigator-reasoning-effort LEVEL Pin the stuck-stage Investigator's model for this run (default, at high: in kilocode runs the run's own direct route outside the stuck stage's model family, never a kilo/ gateway route; otherwise GPT-6 Sol, or GLM 5.3 when the stuck stage runs on Sol). A provider/model id runs it through OpenCode. See Workflow. --utility-model MODEL, --utility-reasoning-effort LEVEL New runs only: run the stages that only classify or reformat (today the Job recognizer, recognize_workflow, which runs only on a flow without Requirements) on a cheaper model. The route keeps the Plan Reviewer's engine, provider and reasoning effort and replaces only the model. Never used for a stage that writes code or judges evidence. Without it every stage keeps its own route. Refused on a saved run. See Models. --resolver-response provide_information --resolver-request ID --resolver-token '…' Answer a Resolver request with --resolver-message TEXT. A displayed criterion recommendation accepts the exact message Accept recommended revision to install an unapproved draft for normal plan review and fresh approval. Other blocker information remains held; operational-exhaustion information is re-evaluated once on resume. Request ID and current token are required. The response launches no provider and grants no approval or budget change (Execution). --close-finding ID --close-reason '…' Close an open reviewer finding as your own decision (repeatable), for example a duplicate of a problem you already settled. Records who closed it and why, and launches no agent. Closing every finding a validation-only stop asked about answers that stop, so the next --resume-paused continues.

docs.title: Waiting or finished
docs.text:
--follow-up continues only a finished run (TASK_COMPLETE). A waiting, paused or blocked run refuses it (exit 2, state unchanged): answer it (--answer/--delegate with --resolver-token), approve or correct it (--approve-goal/--feedback), or resume it. Jobs that report without waiting for a reply (design review, discussion, code review) complete with their questions or findings in their report; you reply to them with --follow-up. After a design turn, "Build it." builds that design as approved (checked against the code first, no requirements gathering or questions, plan approval still required). The build gets a plan of its own: the design turn's plan (which wrote no code), with whatever earlier turns agreed that it carried, and its open non-blocking findings are archived in the run, not revised; the design is now the requirements. After a design review instead, building the design it approved revises the plan in force. A follow-up builds as approved only the design its previous turn wrote, or the design a design review approved; any other document is planned from requirements as usual.

The run is Status view Say the next thing with Through TaskRun finished done is true, needs is null --follow-up TEXT follow_up(text) waiting for you needs.kind is answer, approve_plan, review or planning_budget --answer/--delegate with --resolver-token, --approve-goal, --approve-review, --feedback answer, approve_plan, approve_review, feedback stopped needs.kind is resume autocode resume, once the cause in stop_reason is resolved (--resume-paused after editing the design at PAUSED_DESIGN_CONFLICT) resume_paused() stopped in a workflow job (Reviewer, Architect, Analyst, Investigator) needs.kind is retry_job, or recover_source for an attempt with no saved source identity --resume-paused --retry-failed-stage --job-retry-token TOKEN after inspecting needs.archive; with needs.route (quota, a content-filter refusal or an authenticated output limit), first --answer route-ROLE=MODEL --job-retry-token TOKEN to run it on another model, then the retry with the new token; for recover_source, a new run (Task-run interface) retry_job(token); with needs.route, assign_model(role, model) first waiting on another run needs.kind is dependency --receive-dependency MANIFEST once that run delivers receive_dependency(manifest)

The wrong one is refused with exit 2 and the run left as it was. --follow-up on an unfinished run lists the alternatives (answer, approve or correct, resume). On a finished run, --answer, --delegate or --delegate-all says: "This run is finished and waits for no answer; reply to the questions in its report with --follow-up TEXT", and --feedback, --edit-goal, --goal-file or --reject-assumption says it would reopen the run without a new turn. Without --run-dir, --follow-up is also refused when a run started after the latest finished one has not finished: the message lists that run, and the command that continues the finished one anyway. Through TaskRun these raise TaskRunError.

docs.title: Replying to a design review
docs.text:
A design review never waits for its questions: the run completes with them in review/design-review.json, and you answer with --follow-up ("Ordering is per-domain."). The Architect is asked to keep a concern that is a problem only under one answer to its question advisory until you answer. A reply recognized as design makes the Architect revise the same review instead of writing a new one. It is asked to:

  • keep every earlier concern under its id, open or resolved, and to drop or renumber none;
  • keep a concern the reply settles with status resolved and a resolution saying what settled it (an answer can also make a concern blocking), and to add a concern only for a problem the reply exposes;
  • drop the questions the reply answered and keep the others under their ids.

The runner refuses a revision that leaves out an earlier concern id, uses an id twice, resolves a concern without a resolution or resolves one raised in that revision, or whose verdict is not request_changes exactly when an open concern is blocking. A reply that names a different design gets a fresh review (revision 1); a reply asking for a new design hands it to the build pipeline, as a first request would.

revision is the review's number, and revisions keeps one entry per review: the message that prompted it (said, null for the run's first review), its feedback receipt (event_id), the verdict, and the ids of its open blocking, open advisory and resolved concerns and of its questions. The report you reply to must be the one the Architect wrote: if review/design-review.json was edited since, --follow-up exits 2 with "changed since the Architect's review; restore it or start a new run".

docs.title: Execution and recovery
docs.text:
autocode resume can replace --resume-paused alongside a recovery companion such as --grant-recovery N, --retry-failed-stage, or an explicit budget change. This also works when AutoResolver has published the operational pause as WAITING_FOR_USER, provided its saved request is still valid. Bare resume does not acknowledge that published request; ordinary questions and approvals still require their own actions. Recovery eligibility and token checks are unchanged.

Flag Meaning --resume-paused Acknowledge an operational pause and continue. Does not approve a draft, and does not restore a spent recovery allowance. autocode resume implies it at PAUSED_* (not PAUSED_DESIGN_CONFLICT), BLOCKED_*, *_REWORK_REQUIRED and RESOLVER_PENDING, never with a user action or --resolver-response; with a recovery companion, also at a verified operational pause published as WAITING_FOR_USER. --retry-failed-stage With --resume-paused, authorize one fresh attempt at the recorded repeated failure after inspecting its retained work; no approval or budget bypass. --diagnose-failed-stage With --resume-paused, request bounded read-only diagnosis of a recorded repeated Builder report failure. Alternative to --retry-failed-stage; not a permission or budget override. --grant-recovery N With --resume-paused, authorize N more automatic timeout recoveries for a run paused at PAUSED_TIMEOUT_RECOVERY after its cause was fixed. Audited as a recovery_grant user event; recovery history is retained. --skip-requirements New run, for an unattended worker: wherever Requirements would wait for your answers, each question that --delegate-all could delegate is answered with its proposed default and recorded as delegated (source: skip_requirements). The Planner and Plan Reviewer still run in full; a question with no safe default (cost, quota, permission, external side effect, the requested outcome) still waits for a person, and so does plan approval. A saved run keeps the choice it started with. --skip-to-build New run: --skip-requirements, and once the Plan Reviewer has finalized the plan, approve it and go on to the Orchestrator and building in the same invocation. The approval is recorded as yours, with this checkout's provenance, marked source: skip_to_build in approvals and approved_contract.approval_source; a run's --require-approver still applies. Needs joint planning. Without this flag AutoCode never approves its own plan. --plan-review-full Keep full-depth plan review for this run: the review allowance stays per planning cycle even for a small clear brief (see Milestone checkpoints). --planning-review-call-limit N At a reconciled planning-budget pause, save a total allowance for the current cycle. 0 disables the cap for this and future cycles while preserving usage history; it can also be saved at a requested pause or after abandoning a stopped stage. No model launch or approval; resume separately. --pause-after-stage Stop at the next saved boundary. --verbose / --no-verbose Stream each stage's live model activity (tools started and finished, new model text, one bounded line each) to stderr as Role/model: …. On by default; --no-verbose or AUTOCODE_VERBOSE=0 turns it off. Not saved with the run: each command that runs stages reads it afresh. The full stream is always kept in the stage's iterations/NNN/<stage>-NN.jsonl. --retry-builder M2 With --resume-paused, authorize one retry of the exhausted current serial milestone or stopped parallel members (not a member stopped by its provider's content filter or response output limit: answer its route-terra question; once that request was answered with information or left paused, --retry-builder asks the question again and launches nothing). Keeps failure history, model routes and verification gates; all workers must be stopped. A refused or output-limited member retry with settings saves nothing. A parallel member reruns on its saved Builder route, so a Builder model, provider or reasoning effort change with its retry is refused. A difference saved separately in the run's Builder settings also refuses the retry, naming both routes. Answer that member's open route-terra question to choose its model, or restore the run's Builder settings to the member's route separately before retrying. --reconcile-only TOKEN Metadata-only classification of an unfinished saved RUNNING attempt whose supervisor, keeper and provider are freshly confirmed dead. Take the exact action and private token offered by status; - reads AUTOCODE_RECONCILE_ONLY_TOKEN. A successful saved classification exits 0 while the run remains paused. Records an uncertain-stage pause without configuring, launching, adopting or retrying a provider. Retains work, usage, routes and limits. Refuses a changed checkpoint, live/unknown supervision, pending stop or native visual/durable service execution. Cannot combine with settings or other actions. --abandon-stage '001/terra-01' Archive a stopped attempt, keep partial edits and logs. --retry-report ATTEMPT_ID With --resume-paused, request fresh Tester evidence after report repair or repeated-failure limits stop a rejected report, using the exact attempt ID status names; saved source and evidence pins must still match. After a source edit, --resume-paused validates the current source instead. --accept-transport-change Resume a transport-change pause after route checks. --accept-source-edit With --resume-paused, hand a paused repair the source edited while it was stopped. The resolution's source revision becomes the current snapshot, and a recovery packet bound to the replaced source stays on disk but is detached from the request. The approved contract, task, budget, proof and evidence pins stay. It refuses any other change, and source the Resolver wrote. --export-repair Write the dispatched bounded repair (a run paused with resolution_request + current_task) as handoff/repair-spec.{json,md} beside the run: affected paths, the repair instruction, the binding contract hash, the acceptance criteria and the runnable verification commands. Run state is untouched; the export is also the binding --submit-repair re-checks. --submit-repair DIR Adopt a completed external implementation delivered as a checkout of this repository at the dispatched base with only this repair applied. Re-runs the static gates and the regression proof (including the fail-on-base property), imports the changed files inside the repair's affected paths (rolling the workspace back on rejection), and on success advances the milestone and records the external provenance in user_events; rejection names the failing criterion. --max-parallel-builders N Concurrency limit for independent milestone Builders. --milestone-checkpoints / --request-milestone-checkpoints Enable milestone checkpoints (idle boundary / queued). A --max-milestone-seconds N given with either on a saved run is saved without being recorded as yours: AutoResolver may extend it once and a Builder climb is not projected against it, until a later resume sets --max-milestone-seconds again. See Budget ownership. --max-milestone-seconds N Milestone active-time budget (default 5400; 0 disables). Checked before each writer launch, and, when you set it, before a climbed Builder attempt (its stronger attempt or a climb on its effort ladder) whose projected time, the last Builder attempt's duration, would take the milestone past N: that pause (PAUSED_MILESTONE_BUDGET) names the total, and --resume-paused --max-milestone-seconds M with M at least that total launches the attempt. With --resume-paused it also restarts the milestone's counted time, except under a progressive run's slice budget, which it also sets but whose count it does not restart. See Milestone checkpoints. --max-milestone-replans N Changed-approach replan limit (default 1). --max-milestone-stalled-reviews N Reviews without progress before replanning (default 3; 0 disables). --max-findings-per-task N Cap open findings bundled into one REWORK task. --max-idle-seconds / --max-tool-seconds / --max-stage-seconds Watchdog limits (new-run defaults 300 / 1800 / 3600; 0 disables). On the default idle limit, Requirements, Planner and Plan Reviewer launches run under a 600-second floor and MiMo routes under 900 (see Timeouts and watchdog); a limit you set is used as given. --max-seconds N Total active provider time for the run (new-run default 43200, 12 hours; 0 disables). Checked at stage boundaries, and, when you set it, before an attempt on a stronger route (the Builder's stronger attempt or a role's climb on its effort ladder) whose projected time, the role's last attempt's duration, would take the run past N: that pause (PAUSED_TIME_LIMIT) names the total, and --resume-paused --max-seconds M with M at least that total launches the attempt. See Timeouts and watchdog. --max-cost-usd N A money cap in USD: the run pauses at the next stage boundary once its spend reaches N (no cap by default; 0 removes it), and before any attempt it can price (a job's next attempt, projected from that job's last attempt's tokens at the saved route's rate; the Builder's stronger attempt or a role's climb on its effort ladder, at the stronger route's rate) whose projected cost would take the spend past N, so a stage the run can price never crosses the cap. Spend is the provider's reported cost, else the stage's tokens at the dated price table (autocode models --prices); a stage on a model without a rate, or one whose provider recorded no token counts, is not counted and the cost line says so. The pause is yours to decide (PAUSED_COST_LIMIT): --resume-paused --max-cost-usd M with M above the spend (and at least the cap a stop before a priced attempt names) continues, and AutoCode never raises the cap itself. See Money cap. --no-progress-limit N Unchanged-batch limit (new-run default 3; 0 disables the cap, never the 3-recovery ceiling). With --resume-paused, an N above the retained count, or 0, acknowledges a PAUSED_NO_PROGRESS request, also when N is already saved; it never acknowledges another cause's pause. When the limit caused the pause, its advice names this flag and the retained count, not --resolver-response: information alone never acknowledges it. --max-iterations N Optional total iteration ceiling; new runs default to unlimited, and resumes retain their saved limit. --unlimited-iterations Remove only the iteration ceiling; other safety and usage limits remain. --legacy-iteration-ceiling N Compatibility form of the iteration ceiling, used only when --max-iterations is absent. --autoresolver-managed-limits Delegate finite CLI safety limits to bounded Resolver recovery; never changes billing or model routes. --test-command CMD The project's test suite command for runner-owned regression proof (default: detected). Correct a saved command with --resume-paused at a reconciled pause before the Tester or combined checkpoint, or at a Completion Owner blocker hold; see Bug fixes. --test-report junit:PATH Use one fresh JUnit XML file at a workspace-relative path as named test evidence. Requires an explicit --test-command; when --regression-command is omitted, that suite also runs in the regression proof trees. Every invocation must write the same relative report path; old output is cleared and captured XML is hash-pinned. Saved corrections use the same reconciled pre-validation pause as --test-command. No directory/glob or TRX input. See JUnit proof setup. --test-root components/api/ New runs only: save a plain workspace-relative directory for automatic Python suite detection (pytest or unittest). Fixed at launch, not changeable on resume. Changes outside it remain UNVERIFIED, including with an explicit test command. This selects proof tests, not a general write boundary; identified generated component tasks also bind their declared plan ownership to this caller root. See Scoped Python proof. --package packages/api/ New runs in a monorepo: the repository directory the task works in. Suite detection reads only that directory, and the detected suite, the derived regression command and the original-test replay run from it (cd packages/api && SUITE); an explicit --test-command still runs from the repository root as given (write cd packages/api && … to run it in the package), and the learned project-memory test command is not applied. Only the package's existing tests are retained as original test gates. In a bug fix the Investigator is told the package and its suite, and a diagnosis that names files outside it is refused as invalid output. The package is the Builder's write scope: a change outside it, in any package run, is a blocking runner finding naming each path, checked before each Tester and Completion Reviewer dispatch and by --accept-completion after its own checks (a runner regression proof also leaves it UNVERIFIED); what it leaves out, such as an ignored file the plan does not name or the checkout's own nested repositories, is in the linked section. The directory must hold committed files (an --in-place run: files Git does not ignore). Fixed at launch; not with --test-root. Nothing limits the Builder's writes while it works. See Monorepo packages. --base-patch PATH Bug fixes whose only regression test needs a hook or variable the fix adds: a patch that adds only that instrumentation to the original code, so the test can run and fail there. Pinned by hash, may not change test files, and its edits must occur at the corresponding original source locations in the final change; every proof that uses it asks the Tester and Completion Reviewer to check it changes no behavior. Set it when the run starts, or with --resume-paused at a stop before the Tester or a completion check. --regression-command CMD A command that runs the new or changed tests (default: derived). Multi-milestone features accumulate changed Python test files in supported literal pytest/unittest lists while retaining selectors and options; see Bug fixes. Saved corrections require the same pre-validation --resume-paused boundary as --test-command.

An execution permission question can offer explicit suite/tool/stage timeout changes. Select the exact displayed choice with the normal --answer action; the runner applies that choice's settings and records their old/new values. Declining changes no timeout. These decisions preserve the approved goal and elapsed run budget. Legacy prose-only consent changes no runner setting; see timeout permission payloads.

An accepted parallel --retry-builder copies the run's saved operator tool, stage and milestone bounds (--max-tool-seconds, --max-stage-seconds, --max-milestone-seconds) to only those members. Save these limits separately or beside the retry. Zero keeps its disabled meaning; old attempt deadlines, spent time and recovery allowances remain intact.

docs.title: Engine, provider, and models
docs.text:
Flag Meaning --engine opencode\|codex\|claude Engine for the run. OpenCode is the default; claude runs Claude Code, the built-in claude provider (the OpenCode engine's facade with --provider claude; another --provider is refused). Other tools join as providers (see Providers). --provider <name> External tool registered via TOML (see Providers). --role-transport ROLE=PROVIDER New run on the OpenCode facade engine (any provider, or --engine claude): run one role on another connected tool, never the run's own; repeat for more roles and provide each selected role's explicit model flag. Other roles keep their saved routes. The tool binding is immutable after launch and cannot combine with --single-model or recorded replay. See Per-role tools. --allow-uncontained-tools Built-in OpenCode runs only (including a Codex run whose --investigator-model is an OpenCode provider/model). Without it, a run is refused before any stage when the kernel tool boundary cannot exist here (it needs macOS sandbox-exec or Linux bubblewrap, and OpenCode 1.18.33). With it, every stage, the Planner's read-only shell included, runs with OpenCode's own permission checks only, no kernel containment. Accepted on a new run or a resume (including a PAUSED_TOOL_CONTAINMENT run); saved with the run and recorded as a user event, so later resumes need not repeat it. The status view shows tool_containment. See Execution. --joint-planning Add joint Requirements / Plan Reviewer work. --adaptive-planning / --no-adaptive-planning New runs plan as deep as the job needs by default (joint planning on the default flow): a Plan Reviewer with no blocking concern approves the draft, a large plan gets a third review call, and feedback on a shown plan goes to the Planner. Requirements always runs first. --no-adaptive-planning keeps the fixed sequence; --adaptive-planning insists. See Adaptive planning. --compact-bugfix-planning / --no-compact-bugfix-planning New run, bug fixes only: when the Investigator reproduces the bug with a probe the runner ran, sizes the fix small, names its root cause, invariant and regression cases, touches at most four files and none the project's sensitive-paths name, the runner writes the plan draft itself from the diagnosis and the Requirements record instead of the Planner's paid draft call; the Plan Reviewer reviews that draft and you approve the displayed plan as usual, and a blocking concern returns the run to the Planner. Enabled by default for new joint-planning runs; needs adaptive planning. Without a sensitive-paths declaration, new runs save conservative shipped patterns for authentication, security, payments, billing, migrations, credentials, CI/build files and dependency manifests/locks. Explicit project patterns replace those defaults. The status view's stage_policy records the decision and its reasons (Compact planning for bug fixes). --review-routing separate\|combined New runs only. separate keeps the default Tester followed by Completion Reviewer. combined uses the configured Completion Reviewer model, effort and session for one independent testing/completion call (astra_checkpoint), with the separate Tester available for concrete escalation. This replaces separate enforced milestone-checkpoint routing and cannot be combined with explicit --milestone-checkpoints. The policy is included in the displayed, hashed plan and activated only by approval of that exact plan. Regression proof, changed-code evidence, independent models, required human reviews and limits still apply. Saved runs keep their routing, including across follow-ups. --spec-first / --no-spec-first Off by default. A new run with joint planning on the default flow stops after Requirements every time it produces a handoff: the question (needs.kind answer, id requirements-review-…) shows the outcome, behaviors, acceptance examples, constraints, what was left out and the assumptions. Answer plan to start the Planner, or say what to change and Requirements runs again with your answer. Adaptive planning never skips Requirements on such a run. After plan approval the Tester writes the acceptance tests before the Builder, which may not change them. A saved run keeps its choice. See Spec-first runs. --blind-tests / --no-blind-tests Off by default. Implies --spec-first. The Tester writes acceptance tests before the Builder starts, and the runner archives them in evidence and removes them from the workspace. The Builder gets no prompt note naming them and never sees the test code. Before review and completion, the runner executes them in a candidate scratch tree; any failure becomes a blocking runner finding. See Blind tests. --builder-strong-model MODEL New run: the model for the Builder's stronger attempt after its ordinary retry (default openai/gpt-6-sol, or strong_model under [builder_retry] in the provider config; see Models). Refused when it is the checker model or shares its GLM or MiMo family, and when the run's provider lists its models without it (or without the checker model a Tester or Completion Reviewer on its family would move to). --single-model MODEL New run: use one model for every role, including reviewers; explicitly relaxes cross-model verification for single-subscription accounts and implies joint planning. With a tool that lists its models' reasoning variants (Kilo, OpenCode), a role effort the model does not declare moves to its nearest declared variant before anything launches (said once, recorded as effort_fits); an effort you named with --reasoning-effort or a role's flag is never moved: the run pauses as PAUSED_EFFORT_UNSUPPORTED and names the variants the model declares, which --answer effort-ROLE=EFFORT takes (#2057). See Reasoning effort --auto-select / --no-auto-select New run: choose every role's model from the tool's connected accounts (#1426) - cheapest qualified route per role, checkers independent, the routes still unproven probed at their own reasoning level before the first stage. Per-role model flags, --single-model and role-provider flags still win; a saved run keeps the routes it started with; a selection that cannot field an independent checker refuses to start, in account terms. --no-auto-select is the explicit opt-out. Preview with autocode models --selection. Not yet the default: that flip waits on #1426 step 12's qualification. See Choosing models automatically. --requirements-model, --glm-model, --plan-reviewer-model Planning-role model overrides (bare GPT names). --astra-model, --terra-model, --sol-model, --completion-model Execution-role model overrides (provider/model IDs). --astra-provider, --terra-provider, --sol-provider, --completion-provider Per-role Codex provider override (Responses API); the saved engine stays the same. --reasoning-effort, --astra-reasoning-effort, --terra-reasoning-effort, --sol-reasoning-effort, --completion-reasoning-effort Shared or execution-role reasoning effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). --glm-reasoning-effort, --requirements-reasoning-effort, --plan-reviewer-reasoning-effort Reasoning effort for the Planner, Requirements or Plan Reviewer. --resolver-model, --resolver-reasoning-effort Override the saved Resolver model or reasoning effort without changing its engine. OpenCode-engine runs only: a Codex-engine run, or a saved run without joint planning, ignores them, and its Resolver starts from the astra route (--astra-model). See Models. --pin-model-role astra\|terra\|sol\|completion Keep the selected role model and reasoning effort instead of escalating automatically; repeat for multiple roles. Of these routes only terra, sol and completion have an effort ladder; the Resolver's own route climbs GPT-6 Astra and has no choice here. astra pins the route the Resolver's route is copied from, so on a new run it pins the Resolver too; once a run's Resolver route exists (a Resolver stage ran, or --resolver-model created it), no flag pins it. --migrate-only Run the opt-in legacy migration and stop (see Testing).

Saved model changes (role model flags or answers to a stopped role's model question) print an advisory to stderr when a previously independent Requirements, Planner, or Builder producer/consumer route becomes the same model or GLM/MiMo family. Existing shared links and reasoning-only changes do not repeat it. The advisory describes selected routes for future work; saved artifacts retain their original authorship. It does not block the change or relax the mandatory verifier checks. Different GPT tiers remain distinct, as in those checks.

docs.title: Project settings
docs.text:
A team keeps the settings it would otherwise type on every new run in .autocode/config.toml in the workspace, or, in a Python project, under [tool.autocode] in pyproject.toml (config.toml wins a key both set). Commit the file like any other: the .autocode/.gitignore AutoCode creates leaves config.toml trackable. In a checkout whose .autocode/.gitignore AutoCode created before this, add the line !/config.toml to it, or git add -f .autocode/config.toml.

engine = "opencode"
test-command = "python -m pytest -q"
sol-model = "openai/gpt-6-sol"
terra-reasoning-effort = "high"
max-seconds = 7200

Each key is a flag's name without its leading dashes, and takes the values that flag takes; a switch takes true or false.

Kind Keys Engine engine Review routing review-routing Models single-model, astra-model, terra-model, sol-model, completion-model, glm-model, requirements-model, plan-reviewer-model, resolver-model, investigator-model, builder-strong-model Reasoning efforts reasoning-effort, astra-reasoning-effort, terra-reasoning-effort, sol-reasoning-effort, completion-reasoning-effort, glm-reasoning-effort, requirements-reasoning-effort, plan-reviewer-reasoning-effort, resolver-reasoning-effort, investigator-reasoning-effort Test command/report test-command, test-report Budgets max-iterations, unlimited-iterations, max-seconds, max-cost-usd, max-stage-seconds, max-idle-seconds, max-tool-seconds, no-progress-limit, max-milestone-seconds, max-milestone-replans, max-milestone-stalled-reviews, max-findings-per-task, max-parallel-builders Approvals (no flag) require-approver Development server (no flag) serve Sensitive paths (no flag) sensitive-paths

require-approver has no flag: one plain Git email address, or a list of them, allowed to approve the run's plan and reviews and to accept its completion, such as require-approver = ["lead@example.com", "deputy@example.com"]. A run started with it refuses a plan approval, an artifact acceptance or --accept-completion when git -C WORKSPACE config --get user.email, for the run's saved workspace in AutoCode's own environment, is not listed (compared without regard to case), before anything is approved, and stays at the same stop; an --as name never counts. Without it anyone may approve. No flag sets or overrides it. It guards against an approval under the wrong configured Git identity, not against someone who deliberately sets a listed address (Git's environment variables or a repository-local user.email change what is checked): it is not authentication. A replay never takes it, and autocode components child runs read it from their own worktree, so only a committed file reaches them (Required approver).

serve has no flag either: the command that runs the project's development server, with {port} where the port goes. It is a string, or in .autocode/config.toml a table that also names the path that answers once the server is ready (ready-path, any answer below 400) and how long to wait for it (ready-seconds, 1 to 600, default 60); pyproject.toml takes only the string. A new run saves it with its settings, so an edit to the file, including one the Builder makes, never changes the command a run serves with. Every {port} is replaced with a free loopback port; any other text goes to the shell unchanged.

sensitive-paths has no flag either: a list of shell-style path patterns over repository-relative paths (src/billing/**, *.lock, migrations/) naming the files a shorter planning path may never touch, saved with a new run. The compact bug-fix planning path (--compact-bugfix-planning) takes the full path for a fix whose files match any pattern, and uses conservative shipped patterns when a new run has no declaration. An empty list (sensitive-paths = []) declares that nothing is sensitive. Saved runs keep their existing policy. Matching is by path only; runner-proven reproduction, independent plan review and exact-plan approval still apply (Compact planning for bug fixes).

[serve]
command = "npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port {port}"
ready-path = "/"
ready-seconds = 90

A flag on the command line wins over the file, and over any file key it cannot be combined with: a typed --single-model drops the file's role models, a typed role model drops its single-model, and a typed iteration ceiling drops its max-iterations and unlimited-iterations. The file wins over the built-in default; no environment variable sets these keys. A setting from the file counts as typed, so a budget the team set is never extended as a runner default. A new run prints which settings it took from which file. Only a new run reads the file, including one started from a design handoff with --ui-run and no typed task: a saved run keeps the settings it started with, so changing the file never alters a run in progress.

engine = "claude" is allowed: it selects the built-in Claude Code provider, which runs AutoCode's fixed command line, as engine = "codex" does. A project cannot choose the provider (provider, or a role's astra-provider, terra-provider, sol-provider, completion-provider): it runs a command you installed, so it comes from --provider, AUTOCODE_PROVIDER or default_provider in ~/.config/autocode/config.toml. Nor task-preflight, the operator's prerequisite manifest. A file that names either, an unknown key, or a value its flag would refuse stops a new run before it starts, naming the file and the key. autocode doctor lists each setting a new run would take and the file it came from, and fails on such a file.

docs.title: Project memory
docs.text: Completed tasks save shareable learned project facts in .autocode/project.json. Its test command is a default below flags and both explicit project files (not in a --package run, which neither takes nor saves it); historical human conventions are Requirements context, never new acceptance criteria or approval. Saved runs retain their original snapshot. autocode doctor shows the record and setting sources. autocode forget clears only the learned file. See Project memory for provenance, sharing, the versioned schema and the two-run behavior.

docs.title: Advanced run inputs
docs.text: Flag Meaning --help-all Full run-option help, including advanced controls omitted from the short overview. --unit autoplanner\|autocode\|autoreview\|autoresolver Run one unit and stop before the next; omitting it runs the full controller. --conversation-handoff PATH Attach a validated conversation receipt to a new task; grants no approval. --conversation-session With a creation-only --conversation-handoff, initialize the core conversation before ordinary planning; cannot target a saved run and grants no approval. --conversation-request PATH On a saved run, apply the owned journal-sealed request for its exact --feedback or --answer. Retains the saved acknowledgement for idempotent delivery; grants no approval and starts no provider. --task-preflight PATH Prerequisite manifest for planning, building and validation; saved corrections require its reconciled pause and --resume-paused. --figma-manifest PATH, --figma-additional-file URL Complete immutable multi-file/frame/state references for a new Figma run; repeat additional file URLs as needed. --figma-approved-scope PATH External reviewed product-scope artifact bound to a complete version 2 inventory and its approved cases. Requires --figma-approved-scope-sha256 with new-run --figma-manifest or stopped --revise-figma-manifest. Grants no plan approval; full original-source validation remains required (scope admission). --figma-approved-scope-sha256 SHA256 Trusted operator SHA256 of the exact --figma-approved-scope artifact; required with that option, never inferred from the design bundle. --revise-figma-manifest PATH, --expected-design-hash HASH, --design-change-reason TEXT At a stopped run, propose changed Figma references against the inspected hash, retaining history and requiring plan review. --revise-protected-tests PATH Explicit user revision of the original test inventory and command; requires a reconciled validation pause. The core may offer @approved-suite for a command-only correction that keeps every sealed original test, using the combined suite displayed by chat. A package-collision correction explicitly displays root-first collection and --import-mode=importlib before confirmation. --bind-dependency PATH, --receive-dependency PATH Register an authorized prerequisite or receive its verified delivery manifest; neither approves the plan. --resolver-message TEXT Corrective information accompanying an operational Resolver response. --reconcile-review CRITERION=ANSWER Bind an authenticated legacy acceptance to current validated evidence without granting a new approval. --accept-completion Accept completion only after the runner verifies every gate, when the model completion report cannot be produced. Records who accepted it, as an approval does (Who approved), and a project's require-approver checks it (Required approver). --evidence-provenance fake\|live\|unknown Disclose the run's model-evidence origin; saved with a new run. --context-soft-tokens N, --rotate-after-input-tokens N Context-compaction and checkpointed session-rotation thresholds; 0 disables rotation. --tool-output-mode raw\|conservative Display mode for AutoCode capture/file-read tools; saved across resume. --headroom off\|on Off by default; on refuses to run until compatibility has been verified. --planning-v2 Opt in to transactional planning artifacts; keeps the existing role models and default planning flow.

docs.title: Figma / UI
docs.text: Flag Meaning --build Hand an accepted Figma result to the implementation runner. --figma-file <url> Refine or implement from a specific Figma file. --ui-run /path Import a completed design run. --figma-review human Require a human visual approval during implementation. --max-plan-reworks, --max-reworks Review-loop limits (none, 0, or a number).

docs.title: Development server
docs.text:
autocode serve start runs the project's serve command for a saved run and keeps it in the foreground. AutoCode picks a free port on 127.0.0.1, puts it wherever the command says {port} and in PORT, sets HOST=127.0.0.1, and runs the command in the run's workspace with credentials removed from its environment, under the same process supervision as a test command. Once the server answers (any connection, or a status below 400 at ready-path) it prints Serving http://127.0.0.1:PORT/. Ctrl-C, closing the terminal or autocode serve stop from another terminal stops its whole process group; if the autocode serve start process dies, its supervisor ends the server. A run has at most one server; a second start is refused while one runs.

start follows the run's code. After each code-changing step the run applies (each new code checkpoint), it stops the server and starts it again, on the same port when that port can be bound again, so the address stays the same, and prints Serving http://127.0.0.1:PORT/ again after a code change. It reads the run's state.json for this and never writes it. A pause or the run's completion leaves the server running, so you can try the app while you answer a question, approve a plan or review the result; it stops only when you stop it.

The server never starts, pauses or decides a stage. Its record is dev-server.json in the run directory, and each start keeps its output and supervision receipt under dev-server/. autocode serve status and autocode --status (view.dev_server) show configured, status (off, starting, running, stopped, exited, failed, or lost when the process that served it is gone), the url while it runs, the command, its port, times, exit_code, reason, log, restarts (how many code changes restarted it), code_checkpoint (the code checkpoint it serves) and waiting. A server that exits, or does not answer within ready-seconds, is recorded as exited or failed with its last output, which start prints; start then keeps waiting (waiting is true) and starts it again after the run's next code change, so a step that fixes a broken app brings the preview back. autocode serve stop or Ctrl-C ends the wait. Once the run has completed no step will change its code, so such a server ends start with exit status 1 instead. A run started before its project named serve has none: name it in .autocode/config.toml and start a new run.

docs.title: Subcommand options
docs.text:
These options belong to the command in the first column. A shared spelling can have a different scope: for example, ui --run-dir creates a new artifact directory, while the main run's --run-dir selects a saved run. Every command also accepts -h / --help.

Command Flags Meaning autocode connections --json, --provider, --routes List installed/registered backends, check local credentials without inference, delegate sign-in, or (retired, removed in the next release) configure AutoCode’s direct API-key connection with setup. list and check print one readable line per connection with its state, detail and the autocode connections ... command of each action it offers; --json returns the connection view clients read. list --routes adds the route each role would use, from the connected tool's own model listing (routes[] and routes_lines, or routes_stop), and launches no model; the plain listing names it as routes_next_command. See Connections for clients. autocode modes --json List the run modes a client may offer for a new run: each mode's id, label, description and the start flags to pass. Launches nothing. See Run modes for clients. autocode worker --workspace, --run-dir, --checkpoint, --request-id capabilities reads host admission. launch takes literal core arguments after --, using the selected workspace and exact run destination, a current checkpoint token (or - for a fresh run), and an optional stable request ID. It returns a launch receipt, not completion. inspect ID reads that receipt; launches --workspace PATH [--run-dir PATH] finds retained launches after a lost reply. These reads never replay a dispatch. See Durable local workers. autocode chat --workspace, --run-dir, --mode, --brief, --line, --execution Project (the current directory by default); pick up this saved run instead of the project's only run; the run mode a new run starts with; the brief, for one that starts with - (--brief=-TEXT); the line-by-line prompts instead of the full-screen interface. New-run options follow --. --execution durable_local opts new chats in this invocation into persistent Linux user services; the default is owned. Reattached runs use their saved status mode. autocode attention --workspace, --run-dir, --item-id Its ack command acknowledges the current saved alert using the status/inventory's named argument array. Records only this local OS user's read state; never answers, approves, resumes or launches a model. Repeating the same acknowledged ID reconciles its original receipt. See attention semantics. autocode conversation --workspace, --run-dir, --text, --title, --request-id, --expected-revision, --supersedes-request-id, --question-id, --resolver-token, --expected-plan-token, --timeout Select a conversation/run, queue a human message, explicitly refresh a revision or hand off its reviewed draft; creation provider/model/effort/budget options follow --. On send, --supersedes-request-id queues a correction only for a definitively rejected, unapplied human request, retaining its history; it cannot replace acknowledged input or active delivery. Sending does not advance the run. All commands print JSON. autocode verify --workspace, --base, --branch, --patch, --criteria, --criteria-file, --out, --record, --engine, --provider, --model, --reasoning-effort, --evidence-provenance, --suite-command, --check-timeout, --max-seconds, --max-stage-seconds, --max-cost-usd, --related-profile, --related-profile-sha256, --json Verify an existing change against caller criteria, or read a retained verification and recheck freshness. --max-cost-usd caps independent review cost; the paired related-profile options preserve a coordinating run's pinned role routes and limits. See Standalone verification. autocode coordinate --run-dir, --workspace, --token, --target, --max-cost-usd, --max-planning-cost-usd, --json The anchor run to coordinate, the authorized local checkout to choose, the exact token of the displayed decision, the ambiguous repository target to resolve, a finite whole-set cost cap for budget, and JSON output. status reads; advance performs one durable core step; bind snapshots exact completed member trees into the approved joint plan; approve, choose and cancel take the corresponding named action. At a settled cost stop, budget --token TOKEN --max-cost-usd N takes the current status offer, retains accumulated spend and other limits, and acknowledges only its displayed member cost pause. It cannot waive a check or approve a plan; zero/unlimited, stale, insufficient, active and cancelled requests are refused. planning-budget --token TOKEN --max-planning-cost-usd N explicitly reallocates a total planning allowance inside the unchanged whole-set cap at its named stop. It preserves all prior spend and work, records the prior allocation, launches nothing, and requires a new exact checkpoint; stale/duplicate, active, unpriced, uncertain and out-of-range requests are refused. A separate ordinary cost-pause acknowledgement may still be needed. At a settled cancellation, resume --token TOKEN --max-cost-usd N takes the exact recovery offer without launching a model or approving a plan. It retains prior work and accounting; an explicit zero removes the shared cap and disables the planning allocation limit while retaining their history. Newer cancellations, stale tokens, active/uncertain work, changed sources and incomplete pricing refuse. access checks GitHub delivery readiness without starting a run. Configure shared roots with autocode registry roots add PATH and standalone checkouts with autocode registry repositories add PATH; /repos displays discovery. autocode setup --install, --json Install that hub (opencode or kilocode) with npm without asking when it is missing; report the four backends and what new runs use without asking anything. autocode stages --model, --effort, --backend, --workspace, --json For set, the stage's model (one the backend offers) and reasoning level (one that model takes, or default when it lists none); the backend whose choices to read or change (claude, codex, opencode, kilocode or a configured provider; default: the one a new run takes); the project whose engine setting counts; and the stage view as JSON. autocode doctor --workspace, --engine, --json Project and engine to inspect; optionally print checks as JSON. autocode forget --workspace, --json Clear the selected project's learned record only; configuration and saved runs remain. autocode models --workspace, --provider, --json, --prices, --selection Project/provider model availability and default routes; optionally JSON; --prices shows the dated price table and each default route's rate; --selection shows what automatic selection would choose and why (#1426). autocode review-pr --out, --post, --json New owned review directory, optional COMMENT-only posting after full finding/head admission, and JSON findings/evidence; creation/provider options follow --. autocode review --workspace, --run-dir, --show, --json Saved task workspace and run (otherwise the workspace's only run); text or JSON evidence without decisions. With neither display flag, ask approve/reject/skip for each pending criterion. autocode serve --workspace, --run-dir, --timeout, --json Saved task workspace and run (otherwise the workspace's only run); with stop, seconds to wait for the server to end (default 15); with status, one JSON object. autocode clean-worktrees --workspace, --yes, --json Select the project; remove eligible completed worktrees only with --yes; optionally format output as JSON. autocode bundle --run-dir, --out, --with-diff, --json The run, as the other commands name it (instead of the positional RUN); where to write the archive; add the run's diff of the workspace source; print the archive path and manifest as JSON. autocode prune-run --run-dir, --yes, --json The run, as the other commands name it (instead of the positional RUN); delete the listed settled evidence bytes (manifests, receipts and hashes retained); without it the command only lists; optionally format output as JSON. autocode merge --workspace, --into, --json Select the project and target branch for a delivered task worktree; optionally format result as JSON. autocode checkpoint --workspace, --run-dir, --compare, --restore, --working, --expected-token, --request-id, --json Compare or restore retained code; --working shows what the running Builder has changed so far (display only). Restore requires its exact inspected token; the request ID identifies the action. autocode replay --into, --export Create a replay at an exact fresh run directory in an isolated workspace, or export a bounded recording bundle. Exactly one target is required. autocode replay --recorded-checks, --json Simulate archived checks with --into without current completion or delivery proof; optionally print the result as JSON. Fresh checks are the default. autocode tasks --workspace, --max-parallel, --dry-run, --json Project, concurrent lanes and a read-only manifest preview. autocode runs --workspace, --all, --needs, --json Project whose runs to list; every registered project instead of one; only the runs waiting on a person; rows as JSON. Read-only: each row shows that run's own status and the command it accepts next. autocode events --workspace, --run-dir, --follow, --timeout Project whose saved run to stream, and the run itself (otherwise the workspace's only run); keep printing new events until the run ends the stream; bound a follow to this many seconds. autocode plan --export, --check, --render, --workspace, --run-dir, --json Exactly one of: write the run's plan to this file, read a plan file and print its goal hash, regenerate a plan file's text from its front matter. With --export, the project whose saved run to export and the run itself (otherwise the workspace's only run). --json outputs structured JSON payloads. autocode wait --workspace, --run-dir, --timeout, --json Project whose saved run to wait on, and the run itself (otherwise the workspace's only run); stop waiting after this many seconds; the outcome as one JSON object. autocode components --workspace, --engine, --provider, --joint-planning, --reasoning-effort Project and model routing for each component. autocode components --auto-approve Apply decisions the operator has already delegated; the flag itself supplies no delegation. autocode components --options, --max-advances, --timeout Shell-quoted child flags, maximum CLI advances per component (20) and per-component wall-clock budget. autocode components --integrate, --run-local, --health-timeout, --keep-running, --runtime-evidence-provenance Integration target, Compose smoke checks, readiness deadline, optional retained services and smoke-evidence origin (fake, live, unknown); see local integration. autocode demo --directory Create a new directory for retained offline demo outputs; defaults to a fresh temporary directory. Existing directories are refused. autocode ui --workspace, --run-dir, --figma-file, --from-plan-run Project, new artifact directory, design file and saved accepted UI plan. autocode ui --planner-model, --astra-model, --terra-model, --sol-model, --astra-reasoning-effort Requirements/Planner, Plan Reviewer, Builder and Tester model choices; review reasoning effort. autocode ui --max-plan-reworks, --max-reworks, --dry-run, --build, --no-chat Plan/design rework limits, preview, implementation handoff and noninteractive presentation. autocode compare-baseline --baseline-root, --candidate-root, --normalize-dependency-prefixes, --output Source roots, explicit dependency-prefix normalization and comparison-result output; see baseline comparison. autocode visual-capture --config, --timeout Capture configuration and command deadline (120 seconds). autocode visual-check --workspace, --policy, --policy-sha256, --output Project, source-owned policy and expected hash, and fresh check-output directory. autocode capture --output, --no-compress, --mode, --known-output-sha256 Retained output, full display, raw/conservative display and verified unchanged-output reference; a command follows --. autocode output --store, --mode, --known-sha256, --raw, --start-line, --end-line Retained store, display mode, verified copy reference, raw retrieval and requested line range. autocode registry --max-depth, --directory-budget, --workspace, --run-dir, --json Bound run-registry imports or select a run;
