see Registry API. autocode registry roots discover --max-depth, --directory-budget, --json Bound source-repository discovery; the result includes completeness diagnostics and catalog/source snapshot identities. autocode registry roots add\|remove --json Add or remove one canonical source root. autocode registry roots list --json List configured source roots and standalone repository registrations. autocode registry repositories add\|remove --json Register or remove one standalone committed checkout. autocode registry repositories list --json List source roots and standalone repository registrations. autocode intervention --workspace, --run-dir, --request-id, --kind, --text, --json Select a run, identify a feedback/pause/stop request and supply text; optionally JSON. autocode issue --project, --remote, --issue-file, --note, --base, --pr-base, --open, --ready, --path, --chat, --no-chat Project and remote; optional offline issue and extra guidance; start/PR bases; explicit push/open and ready-for-review controls; with plan, where the plan file goes in the repository (default plans/issue-N.md). For start and continue, --chat enters terminal chat when input is needed (default with terminal stdin/stdout); --no-chat returns the status and next action instead. See GitHub issues. autocode arena --arena Arena store (default .autocode/arena). autocode arena --repository, --base, --issue, --issue-file, --note, --oracle, --reference, --check, --split Ingest a case with its pinned repository, request, oracle/reference, checks and development/regression/holdout split. autocode arena --cohort, --runner, --option, --fixture, --i-authorize-live-model-spend, --approve-benchmark-plans, --timeout, --oracle-timeout Run/report/propose controls: cohort, runner checkout, repeated child options, fake or explicitly authorized live run, plan approval and deadlines. autocode arena --baseline, --candidate Cohorts to compare. autocode arena --report, --reviewer Annotate a completed attempt from an attribution JSON report; an explicit independent reviewer is required to confirm a diagnosis. autocode unattended --analyze --analyze, --run-dir, --workspace, --out Read-only run analysis; optionally save its evidence report in --out. autocode dashboard --workspace, --watch-root, --watch-depth, --runner, --port, --provider Repeated projects and discovery roots, discovery depth (3), CLI runner, local port (8765) and provider for new runs. autocode changeset --run-dir, --target, --workspace, --set-token, --in, --reason, --message, --json The source run (with every other action: any run of the change set), the repository as its scope.external_parts names it (with reopen and pr-body: the run to act on), the registered project to start the linked run in, the approval.set_token that status showed (- reads AUTOCODE_CHANGESET_TOKEN), the run whose workspace the integration command runs in, a waiver's reason, a follow-up's text (default: the failed check's output), and JSON output. Arguments after -- are the linked run's run options with link, and the integration command with check-command. order takes every run's repository name, first to merge first. autocode bridge --once, --project, --poll-seconds, --json With run: one poll then exit (for tests and cron-style operation), the persistent checkout to build in (default: AUTOCODE_BRIDGE_PROJECT or the daemon's directory) and seconds between polls (default 10, or AUTOCODE_BRIDGE_POLL_SECONDS); with status, JSON output. See Channel bridge.

docs.title: Terminal chat
docs.text:
autocode chat --execution durable_local "YOUR TASK" opts a new run into the durable local worker mode on a supported persistent Linux host. The core checks an existing systemd user manager (254+) and existing linger policy; it never configures them. Normal quit, Ctrl-D, terminal closure and SSH disconnect leave that worker running. Reopen with autocode chat --run-dir RUN. Repeated Ctrl-C requests only the current boundary pause, without escalating to worker termination. This does not change ordinary owned-worker behavior or migrate saved runs. While the current view advertises durable detach support, /open, /new, /tab and the tab keys are available during work. The worker being left continues independently. Returning to an idle boundary reads status and waits for explicit Continue.

Within this terminal session, each of the most recent 32 run identities keeps its transcript, unsent draft and cursor, scroll, log filter and panel choices. Titles are display text; workspace and run paths select the context. Switching always reads fresh core status before a decision. A changed question or plan keeps its earlier draft in input history for explicit recovery with Up, rather than filling the new question automatically. Pending restore confirmations and queued keys never transfer between runs. If a target disappears or cannot be read, Enter retries its status and /runs, /open or /tab selects another; typed text cannot submit a task decision while status is unavailable.

/new opens a local request composer; no core run or tab is created until a brief is submitted. An empty request returns to the original context. Unsent drafts and view choices live only in this TUI process. After restart, saved core conversations, registered runs and existing project input history remain; session drafts, scroll and filters do not.

autocode chat is the terminal client of the task-run interface, beside the VS Code extension and the browser dashboard. It reads only autocode --status, autocode runs --json and runs --all --json (your chats, in this project and every registered one) and autocode modes list --json (a new run's mode), shows the conversation the view carries (view.chat), and acts only through the view's named actions: next_command, the chat.input message offer and the pause offer. The rules it reads them by are in tools/autocode_client_actions.py, the same ones the extension (vscode-extension/src/core/next-command.ts) and the headless conformance client follow, so a person gets the same choices in each:

  • Requirements asks in its own words; you reply in yours, and confirm the understanding it summarizes with y. Before the plan is prepared the chat shows the core's spend confirmation (review.spend_confirmation: what planning spends) and asks Prepare plan? [y/N]; anything but yes sends nothing. A mode that could plan at once (spend_confirmation start; the core lists none since quick was removed on 2026-10-22) would ask Start it? [y/N] before the run starts instead, as the VS Code extension does.
  • A question with options takes the option's number or your own answer; Enter takes the proposed default when there is one.
  • The plan is shown from displayed_plan and approved with y only while its token is still the one shown; anything else you type is sent as plan feedback.
  • A stop only you decide (a pause, a stopped job) says why and continues only on your y; a Resolver request takes your reply.
  • When the run completes you can type a follow-up, or press Enter to finish.
autocode                            # in a terminal: pick up the open run, or ask what to do
autocode chat "Add a --verbose flag to greet.py"
autocode chat                       # the same as plain autocode in a terminal
autocode chat --mode full "Fix the README typo" -- --engine claude
autocode chat --line                # the line-by-line prompts, even in a terminal

In a terminal the chat takes the whole screen: a wordmark splash, the conversation in a scrollable transcript with a colored label for each speaker (PgUp/PgDn), the current question or activity above a boxed composer, and a hint bar. The composer is labeled New chat when typing there starts a run and Reply when it answers the run (Up/Down for history, Ctrl-W/Ctrl-U to edit, Enter to send, Ctrl-D to leave). A paste stays in the composer as one reply, line breaks included, until you press Enter. A plan, a question or a stop is shown where it is asked, and Ctrl-C keeps its meaning: the first asks the run to pause after the current step, the second interrupts it. When the chat ends, its last words stay on the terminal: an error, where to pick the run up, or the command a stop leaves for you to run. --line keeps the plain prompts, and scripts get them automatically when there is no terminal.

In a terminal at least 100 columns wide, a side panel shows the run beside the conversation once it has a plan: where it is and what it needs from you, the current step and its last few attempts (the view's chat.progress), what the running step is doing (the commands it runs, the files it edits and the tools it calls, from the view's chat.activity), each requirement and task with its state, open problems, and a log of how the run moved (a stage starting or finishing, an attempt finishing, a command run, a file edited, a task done, a requirement checked). The status row under the conversation names the newest command or edit, in any width. A command that exited 0 is shown as run, not as passing: only the requirement checks say what passed. Everything in it comes from the status views the chat already reads.

While AutoCode works, a live log under the conversation shows what each running agent is thinking and doing as it happens: its reasoning (∴), its messages (»), the commands it runs ($), the files it edits (±) and the other tools it calls, each line led by the agent's name (Builder · task M2, Plan Reviewer). Parallel Builders each appear under their own name. It comes from the view's chat.log, is refreshed with each status read (every two seconds) and keeps the last 500 entries; the composer stays below it, so you can keep typing commands. It shows on its own in a terminal at least 24 rows tall once an agent is working. Reasoning is shown on one line with its newest words, and tool output is never shown. Like the activity rows it is display only: a thought is not a report and a command shown is not a passed check.

Type / in the composer for commands, at a question or while AutoCode works. The menu narrows as you type; Up/Down choose, Tab completes and Enter runs the highlighted one:

Command What it does /plan, /tasks, /log Show the requirements, the task list or the run's log in the conversation /details Why the run is where it is, verification and recovery evidence, recorded timings, cost coverage, token usage, actual attempt routes and saved routes for future attempts /diff List the saved code steps with the files each changed; /diff N shows the files and the diff changed since step N /undo N At a question: go back to saved step N. It shows what differs and asks first; yes makes a new run on a new branch, your branch and its later work stay as they are, and the chat carries on with the new run, which checks every requirement again /changeset For a run linked with runs in other repositories (autocode changeset link): every run of the change set and its state. Once every run waits on a complete plan it shows each plan and asks before approving them together; once every run is complete and an integration check is due it asks before running it. Nothing else is offered: linking, the check command, waivers, reopening and the merge order stay autocode changeset commands /runs Your chats in every project, open and finished, grouped by project: this project first, then the others by their latest activity, newest chat first in each. Each shows its request, its state and when it last moved; a chat whose run was removed is left out and counted. Chats of one change set are marked and listed together at the end. Also at the first "What do you want done?" /open N At a question, or during detachable durable work: open chat N from /runs, restore its session context and read current status before carrying on. The chat left keeps its worker lifetime /new At a question, or during detachable durable work: compose a new request (also Ctrl-T); an empty request returns to the original chat /tab N At a question, or during detachable durable work: switch to tab N (also Ctrl-←/Ctrl-→); a tab Ctrl-T opened can be left the same way before its request is sent, since nothing runs there. Once a session has two chats, a tab bar under the header lists them with a mark for each: ● working, ! needs you, ✓ done /repos Show configured source roots and discovered repositories. Configure locations once with autocode registry roots add PATH or autocode registry repositories add PATH; bugs need no per-task repository list. See multi-repository setup. /mode [ID] The modes the core lists (autocode modes list; only full since 2026-10-22), and which one new chats start in; /mode ID changes it for new chats only, and a saved mode the core no longer lists gives way to its default /engine [NAME] The engine new chats run on: opencode, codex or claude, set as the VS Code extension's engine picker sets it /connect [NAME check\|login\|setup\|use] The backends autocode connections list reports, with their state. check runs the connection's own check; login and setup hand the terminal to the backend's sign-in or AutoCode's setup and bring the chat back afterwards; use makes new chats use it. Only an action the connection offers is run /stages [STAGE N LEVEL] Each stage's model and reasoning level for new chats, from autocode stages list --json (Choosing each stage's model). In the full-screen chat it opens a drawer with one list per stage: Up and Down move, Enter opens the stage's models (one the stage may not run is shown with the reason and cannot be picked), then that model's reasoning levels, and saves the choice; Esc goes back. The line-by-line chat lists the stages with numbered models and takes /stages builder 2 medium. It lists the backend new chats run on (/engine, /connect … use). Chats already started keep their own /panel Show or hide the side panel /live [NAME\|thinking\|messages\|tools\|all\|off] Show or hide the live agent log. With a word it keeps only one agent (any part of its name, such as M2 or reviewer) or one kind of entry; all shows everything again and off hides it. Where the terminal is too short for it, the newest entries are printed in the conversation /attention or F8 Inspect current saved questions, decisions and completed turns across registered projects, even before selecting a chat. a acknowledges the selected alert, Enter opens its chat, r requests a refreshed snapshot and Esc returns to the original draft and cursor. Acknowledgement leaves the task's answer or plan approval pending. Unavailable inventory and unknown read state remain visible. /pause While AutoCode works: ask it to pause after the current step, as the first Ctrl-C does /help List the commands /quit At a question: leave the chat; the run stays as it is

The side panel's Usage section shows the accounted subtotal, missing prices or usage, active/pending attempts and any configured accounting cap. /details separates provider-reported figures, dated-table estimates and historical comparison estimates; subscription/API-equivalent estimates are not the subscription invoice. Cache and reasoning counts are shown as subsets of input and output, never added twice. Historical attempt models and efforts come from their launch records, while saved routes describe future attempts. Missing fields in older cores remain unknown. Displaying this information calls no model and changes no route, cap or workflow.

The header keeps a last-read status visible while you read history; new background messages do not move the history viewport. If the current tab's read fails, the header says the previous read is being shown. It separates the viewer's successful read age (local monotonic time) from the core snapshot's sample time. /details shows the full sample timestamp and opaque checkpoint/workspace/run identity. Missing or mismatched optional metadata stays unknown. A new poll can refresh the local receipt while the core checkpoint stays identical; neither timestamp is a worker-liveness check, evidence acceptance or meaningful work progress. Failed reads retain the last snapshot under a last-known label; a fresh read clears that read error. No ETA or completion percentage is inferred.

A Plan path section appears for a bug-fix run that recorded which planning path it took (the status view's stage_policy, compact planning): compact: Planner draft omitted with what covers the omission (the runner's draft, the Plan Reviewer, your approval, the regression proof), or full: every planning stage runs with the first reason the full path was kept, and where a review fell back to it. /details lists every reason, the decision rows and the hashes the decision rests on. It renders the core's record and offers no action.

The Verification section and /details distinguish the core's current delivery gate from report inspection. A recorded PASS can be unchecked or stale, and a verified delivery can still have a report not explicitly inspected by that status request. Criteria show their recorded results, supplied coverage state, pending human acceptance and evidence references. Retained edits and successful commands alone do not establish accepted evidence. Recovery details show the core's reason, retained work and offered actions; /diff remains the way to inspect saved changes. Recorded execution, observed interval wall time, current-attempt duration and answered-request waiting are shown only where the core supplies those measurements; missing durations stay unknown, and overlapping categories are not added together.

A command never answers the question that is waiting. To send a reply that starts with /, type //. /diff and /undo take only the compare and restore actions the status view names for a saved step (Saved code checkpoints); the view offers going back only at a pause it can restore from, and /undo says why when it cannot.

The first screen says what a new chat starts with (New chats: Full · OpenCode). A choice made with /mode, /engine or /connect … use is kept for the project in .autocode/chat-settings.json; options after -- on the command line take its place for that chat. While Requirements writes its reply, the reply grows on screen as it is written (the view's streaming message). The terminal rings its bell when AutoCode has worked and now needs you, and a chat you opened earlier in the session is checked while AutoCode works: when it starts to wait for you or finishes, the chat says so.

autocode in a project with earlier chats says how many there are. Up/Down recall your earlier requests and messages in this project, across chats: they are kept, the last 100, in the project's .autocode/chat-history.jsonl once a run has made that directory (a bare y, n or option number is not kept).

The older inline chat (--chat, the default when autocode "TASK" runs in a terminal) still works and is being replaced by this client. Scripts that call plain autocode without a terminal are unchanged.

docs.title: Unattended callers (agents)
docs.text:
autocode unattended (or the internal compatibility wrapper autocode-unattended / scripts/autocode-unattended from a checkout) runs AutoCode for another agent without letting that agent make the operator's decisions. It takes AutoCode's own arguments but refuses every decision or recovery flag (--answer, --delegate*, --approve-*, --resume-paused, --retry-*, --feedback, --follow-up, --accept-completion, --close-finding, --close-reason, --resolver-response, …, including abbreviations) and every flag that sets operator policy instead of a person: --skip-requirements (answers Requirements questions by default), --skip-to-build (approves the plan), --allow-uncontained-tools (lifts the tool boundary) and --accept-source-edit. Setup, routing and start-time budgets (--max-seconds, --unlimited-iterations, model flags) stay allowed. The two classes are DECISION_FLAGS and START_FLAGS in tools/autocode_decision_flags.py; a test fails when a parser flag is in neither, the command word resume (on a paused or blocked run it stands for --resume-paused; a bare relaunch still continues a run that is not paused) and the intervention, tasks, ui, registry, capture and compare-baseline subcommands. It forces --no-chat with no stdin, and when AutoCode stops it prints --status and tells the caller to report and stop. Exit codes are AutoCode's.

When a run completes, the wrapper prints the command to analyze it: autocode unattended --analyze --run-dir RUN [--out DIR]. That launches no stage; it reads the saved run and reports the outcome, each acceptance criterion with its recorded status and evidence, findings, stages (role, time, exit, tokens, report path), cost by role (model calls, seconds and tokens per role, with report-format repair calls counted separately), and the code changes against the task's base commit, including new untracked files, plus a summary of the run's always-on activity log. --out saves analysis.md, the full changes.diff and a copy of activity.jsonl.

To lock a Claude Code agent to it, launch the agent from a copy of examples/agent-operator: its .claude/settings.json allows only autocode-unattended and read-only tools, denies edits and other AutoCode or provider commands, and uses dontAsk so anything else is refused without a prompt. Its CLAUDE.md has the agent report stops verbatim and, after completion, analyze the work read-only. Keep that directory outside the target workspace.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Outcome When What --json prints 0 completed The task completed: view.done is true. The status payload; with result when the invocation also acted. 0 saved A user action (an approval, answer, review decision, feedback and the like) was saved. The status payload plus result, whose saved is true. 0 read A read printed what it read: --status, runs, or events without --follow. That output; --status prints the status payload. 2 stopped The run stopped short of completing: it waits on a person (a question, an approval, a review, a requested pause) or on its environment, a provider or AutoCode. view.pause_category says whose action it needs and view.next_command what answers it. wait also exits 2 for a stopped run, and for endings that are not stops (below). The status payload; with result unless the run printed the payload itself as it stopped. wait --json prints its own outcome object instead (below). 2 refused The input was refused and not saved. A new run refused for a setting may already have created its task worktree and branch (without --in-place). For a refused action on the loaded run, or a setting the run's configuration refuses (such as --single-model or --spec-first on a saved run, or --allow-uncontained-tools where it does not apply; the --json option above lists more), the status payload plus result, whose error.code is input_rejected; for a refusal before the run loads, or a setting refused before a new run's first checkpoint, that result alone. A refused setting still ends stderr with autocode: …. A native visual run saves a refused setting as a PAUSED_INVALID_OUTPUT pause instead (stopped, error null). 2 usage The arguments did not parse, or a later check of them ended with argparse's error. Nothing on stdout: argparse's usage text on stderr.

autocode wait only watches a run, and its outcome says why the wait ended. It exits 0 for complete. It exits 2 for needs_you (the run waits on you) and stopped (the run stopped otherwise), and also for three endings that are not stops of the run: controller_lost (the saved status says RUNNING but nothing owns the run), timeout (--timeout elapsed first) and unreadable (the checkpoint could not be read). It also exits 2 when it cannot tell which run to wait on (none is saved, or several are and no --run-dir names one), with autocode wait: … on stderr and nothing on stdout. Otherwise wait --json prints that outcome object (outcome, status, reason and, when it has one, next_command), never the status payload.

tests/test_json_contract.py holds the CLI to this table on a fake run that stops only to wait on you (view.pause_category is your_decision): at a requested pause (--pause-after-stage), a question, the plan approval and a human review, then it completes. At each stop the test runs --status, a plain relaunch, the command view.next_command offers (resume, answer, approve the plan, approve the review), that command with stale tokens, wait --json, runs --json, events and a usage error. It validates each status payload the main command prints under --json or --status against status-view.schema.json, and the lone {"result": …} against its properties.result. It validates each events line against run-event.schema.json, and checks that wait --json and runs --json, which print their own shapes, report the same status and next_command as the status view. The fake run never stops for its environment, a provider or AutoCode. tests/test_json_output.py covers those: the iteration and time limits (AutoCode), and a saved auth or rate-limit pause (your_environment / model_or_provider) under --status and --json.

Because 2 has several meanings, scripts should prefer --json: view.done, view.needs and view.pause_category say which outcome it was, and after an action result.saved and result.error.code say whether it was saved or refused. The exit codes stay 0 and 2 for compatibility.

docs.title: Subcommand exit codes
docs.text:
Subcommands exit 0 on success, 1 on a domain check or operational failure, and 2 when a run stopped short, input was rejected, or command arguments failed parsing. Under --json, results or error codes are reported in structured JSON.

Subcommand Exit code 0 Exit code 1 Exit code 2 autocode plan Plan exported, verified matching front matter (--check), or rendered (--render). — Stale plan text (stale_plan_text), missing plan error (plan_error), or usage error. autocode prune-run Settled evidence bytes pruned (--yes) or listed in dry run. — Active stage refusal (stage_active), or usage error. autocode merge Worktree branch fast-forward merged into base. Merge refused (branch not delivered or diverged). Ambiguous worktree argument, or usage error. autocode clean-worktrees Completed worktrees removed (--yes) or listed in dry run. Worktree removal failed with error. Usage error. autocode checkpoint Checkpoint inspected (--compare) or restored (--restore). — Checkpoint refused (checkpoint_refused), or usage error. autocode tasks Flow completed (COMPLETE) or dry-run validated. — Flow stopped (PAUSED, WAITING, BLOCKED, FAILED), or usage error. autocode wait Watched run completed (view.done is true). — Watched run stopped (needs_you, stopped), timeout, lost controller, or usage error. autocode doctor Environment, engines, tools and dependencies are ready. Check missing or not ready. Usage error. autocode models Models available and default routes verified. Missing required default model route. Usage error. autocode verify Verified criteria passed and evidence produced. Verification checks failed. Criteria invalid, run error, or usage error.

See also: Install · Workflow · Execution

docs.title: Exact tool output
docs.text:
Use --tool-output-mode raw|conservative for AutoCode capture/file-read display. autocode output read FILE returns exact sections with retained originals; autocode output retrieve SHA256 --raw recovers exact bytes. See exact output transport for options, recovery and measurement limits. Native provider tools keep their existing behavior.

A failed read-only workflow job exposes an exact retry_job action in status. After inspecting the archived attempt, retry with --resume-paused --retry-failed-stage --job-retry-token TOKEN using its current needs.job_retry_token. Plain resume does not repeat the job. Unrestored source blocks retry until the exact original source is restored. The CLI verifies file bytes, modes and Git HEAD even when a capture artifact is missing; changed model/limits still invalidate the retry. An older attempt with no saved original identity exposes recover_source and an explanation instead of a retry action. Inspect its archive and current changes before starting a new run.

For an authenticated hard stage timeout, an operator can preserve the selected model and save a larger finite deadline with --job-retry-token TOKEN --max-stage-seconds N, without resume or retry flags. This changes only that deadline, leaves the job paused and issues a fresh retry token. It preserves total time and money caps, usage, approved plans and source bindings. It refuses idle or tool timeouts, a stale attempt/source/token, a non-increasing deadline and mixed configuration changes. Inspect fresh public status, then retry separately with the new token. This is a public CLI recovery; the status view does not yet offer a deadline editor to clients.

A failed Builder classification can also offer retry_job for the Investigator at PAUSED_BUILDER_CLASSIFICATION. Inspect needs.retained_evidence and use the current needs.job_retry_token through AUTOCODE_JOB_RETRY_TOKEN with --resume-paused --retry-failed-stage --job-retry-token -. Run this retry separately from feedback, approval, source acceptance or abandonment. It starts one fresh read-only investigation of the same task, contract, source and failure; any queued Resolver proposal stays unassigned until the normal classification policy accepts the new diagnosis. Previous failures, repair counts, approvals, Builder allowances and time limits remain in force. Status offers --edit-goal FILE and requires fresh approval when a remaining failure or classification limit prevents retry. Older checkpoints that discarded the failed request also require a plan correction or a new run; plain resume cannot reconstruct the missing proposal.

A job its provider's content filter refused (PAUSED_CONTENT_FILTER) or that ran out of quota (PAUSED_BUDGET) pauses the same way, and its stop names the cause and the model. The same model is likely to refuse again, so needs.route carries the job's model question. --job-retry-token is accepted without --resume-paused --retry-failed-stage only together with that answer: --answer route-ROLE=MODEL --job-retry-token TOKEN checks the model the way a launch would, records a route_assignment and issues a new token for the new model. The old token stops working, and the exact retry with the new token is the only way on: --resume-paused --retry-failed-stage --job-retry-token NEW_TOKEN. After a refusal, until a model is named, the status view's needs.action is that answer and the recovery card offers no retry, since the exact retry would replay the refused model. The Architect, Analyst and Investigator have no --ROLE-model flag, so this answer is how they move. The answer changes only that model: given with a limit or another role's model, with or without its token, it is refused and nothing is saved. It issues a new token, so it is given on its own: next to --resume-paused --retry-failed-stage it is refused before anything is read or saved. At that stop --abandon-stage is refused, and a --ROLE-model flag for the stopped role is refused with this advice instead of being saved (saving it would make the retry stale); only a flag that puts back the model the retry is bound to is saved. The same flag is refused while the job's attempt is still uncertain, including with --abandon-stage in the same command: run --abandon-stage ATTEMPT alone, then answer with the token it shows. After a quota stop, the unchanged retry with the shown token also works once the quota resets. A stopped stuck-stage Investigator (investigate_stuck) accepts route-stuck_investigator: its answer saves both the preparation pin and the current route, then issues a new exact-retry token. Use that token for the retry. Changing --investigator-model alone at this stop is refused before saving settings. An older Investigator stop can expose the same question only when its retained attempt, launch configuration and original source establish that model. Other older job stops without a saved model question keep their exact retry.

docs.title: Standalone verification
docs.text:
autocode verify accepts --workspace, --base, either --branch or --patch, and either --criteria or --criteria-file. Criteria are explicit JSON; they are never inferred. --out names a fresh output directory. --record reads an existing verification and checks freshness instead of running models or checks. Review controls are --engine, --provider, --model, --reasoning-effort, --evidence-provenance, --max-seconds and --max-stage-seconds. The paired --related-profile and --related-profile-sha256 inherit saved review routing and provenance. They refuse explicit --engine, --provider, --model, --reasoning-effort or --evidence-provenance flags rather than silently discarding them. Time and cost caps may still bound the review. --suite-command selects the proof suite and --check-timeout bounds each runner command. --json emits the verdict and evidence metadata. See Standalone verification for the criteria format, proof modes and exit codes.

autocode modes list lists the run modes a client may offer for a new run (--json for the version-1 list). See Run modes for clients.

autocode connections list|check|login|setup manages backend setup; list and check return status without inference, and login delegates to the backend in a terminal. connections setup (retired with the direct connection, #2049) ends by naming the route each role will use, and connections list --routes --json returns the same choice as routes[] — both read the connected tool's own model listing and launch no model. See Connections for clients.

docs.title: Compatibility preparation
docs.text:
The Headroom pilot's HEAD-only compatibility copy omitted the candidate's untracked regressions. A green old suite therefore failed to qualify the actual candidate. autocode_compat_prep.prepare provides an opt-in, model-free path that first copies the candidate's dirty and untracked inputs into a detached worktree, then applies the complete immutable overlay. It leaves the generic autocode_verify.make_tree patch-first behavior unchanged for its other callers.

Pass the expected SHA-256 of the complete patch as overlay_sha256, the required original and candidate nodeids as expected_nodeids, and the selected test files or suite command. The helper checks the pin before applying the patch; even a cleanly applicable hunk-boundary truncation fails this check. Missing required nodeids and a partial explicit candidate change map are rejected before constructing a proof. Adapter paths must stay inside the validation copy; absolute paths and escapes cannot write the original checkout. Use a destination outside the candidate workspace, or a fresh directory below .autocode/scratch/. The candidate itself, its ancestors, source subdirectories and existing in-workspace scratch data are rejected before any copy or cleanup, including symlink aliases. Required nodeid iterables are materialized once; an empty iterator is rejected just like an empty list, before an old-only suite can appear green. The same pinned byte snapshot supplies Git's path accounting and application. Quoted filenames and both ends of renames are accounted for. A patch changed during preparation is rejected instead of certifying different applied bytes.

The helper records the candidate input hashes before overlay separately from the copy hashes after overlay, along with candidate file modes. Patch-touched inputs must retain the complete overlay, including mode-only changes; independent changes to different behaviors in the same file compose and are exercised together. Pinned Git modes are checked for every overlay target, including files the candidate did not edit; a passing suite cannot hide an erased permission change.

Intentional copy-only adapters are explicit transformations entries with a path, transformation callable and rationale. Their before/after hashes occupy a separate receipt section. The synthetic local-operator adapter changes caller qualification without weakening test assertions. Its five tests pass; a broken active-credential policy still fails both added regressions while all three original guards pass. Foreign caller credentials are not adopted, and absent operator credentials produce no usage requests in the fixture.

The executed proof distinguishes FAIL from INCOMPLETE. The unadapted correctly assembled fixture reports three original passes and the two added T3/T5 failures as FAIL. Missing, skipped or deselected required nodeids, omitted candidate files, unbound inputs and an incomplete overlay are INCOMPLETE, even if an old suite was green. A nonzero selected-suite exit cannot be PASS. Failed copy or overlay construction cleans up its worktree and preserves the candidate revision.

write_receipt creates a unique file with exclusive creation on each call. Prior FAIL receipts remain immutable, including when the same result is written again within the same second. Each execution gets a unique log directory, so a later PASS cannot overwrite a log referenced by an earlier FAIL receipt. Evidence and run output belong in ignored output directories, not in commits.

.venv/bin/python -B -m unittest tests.test_compat_prep tests.test_compat_pilot
.venv/bin/python -B -m unittest tests.test_architecture
.venv/bin/python -B tools/run_suite.py --changed --jobs 2
.venv/bin/python -B scenarios/run.py run --fake

These maintained offline controls qualify preparation, nodeid accounting and the synthetic adapter. Real application and live-model evidence is separate.

docs.title: Real application qualification, October 3, 2026
docs.text:
The follow-up for #223 used the original Headroom source 8538a831531bb277a6083ed2a010312a849c3050, its historical candidate production and test changes, and the complete #3863 overlay at 2d764f3eb6b0e558ebd71c0222d15dac53910fcc. Candidate hashes and the complete overlay pin are recorded separately from the two-line validation-copy adapter. The original candidate remains unchanged.

The actual application checks produced these distinct results:

  • The unchanged T3/T5 tests pass on the pre-overlay API.
  • The complete unadapted compatibility copy executes all 258 required cases: 256 pass and exactly T3/T5 fail.
  • Adding explicit local-operator provenance to those two synthetic calls, without changing assertions or other callers, passes all 258 cases with no skips or missing cases.
  • Deliberately disabling learned-token fallback fails T3/T5 and an existing tracker success test; the other 255 cases pass. The adapter does not hide that real behavior defect.
  • Omitting candidate tests and truncating the pinned overlay are each rejected as INCOMPLETE before they can earn compatibility credit.
  • The selected suite includes foreign/forwarded-caller guards, absent-operator behavior, and actual Uvicorn/current PyO3 integration. The loaded compiled core is hash-bound, with its 228 selected native build inputs matched against the original qualified build. Ruff and format checks pass on all eight changed Python files.

A fresh AutoCode review run using OpenCode and openai/gpt-6-sol independently inspected the adapter and executed the same 258-case native application suite. Its report approved the adapter with no findings. The executed receipt has exact case accounting, no skips, the pinned loaded core, and zero refused network attempts. All pinned qualification inputs remained unchanged.

This qualification uses synthetic application credentials, fresh per-test state, pinned local tokenizer assets, and the documented opt-out from upstream health probes. It makes no real vendor API calls. An initial invalid setup let an upstream fixture clear isolation settings and changed the local savings ledger's modification time; without a pre-run copy, its content change cannot be established. That run is excluded and retained. Corrected runs guard access to real application/account files and preserve both ledger bytes and modification time relative to the post-error pin. Intermediate environment failures and blocked background-network attempts are also retained, not relabeled PASS.

The original pilot FAIL and every subsequent result remain separate in ignored .scenario-runs/remaining-defect-proof/headroom-223/ evidence. These results qualify the compatibility preparation and adapter for this pinned application case. The review task's completion does not establish completion or acceptance of the whole Headroom #3913 implementation pilot or reliability across all models and projects.

docs.title: Continuous requirements and Planner boundary
docs.text: A conversation has two independent outputs: the Requirements Gatherer replies to the human, and the Planner produces a structured draft for the exact human turn and requirements revision. A Gatherer reply does not make a plan fresh. The repository-aware Plan Reviewer must still review the final contract before the human can approve it and choose Build.

docs.title: Adapter contract
docs.text:
tools/dashboard/planner_dispatch.py is the structured Planner adapter. Its provider receives the transcript, selected route, work directory, logical turn ID and requirements revision. Dispatch observers retain process, provider and result events. The production adapter uses a fresh OpenCode session with all tools denied; malformed output, incomplete provider events, tool calls and model-route mismatches fail without inventing a draft.

Every accepted draft passes validate_structured_result. The versioned schema is documented in docs/schemas/continuous-planner-contract.schema.json and shipped in tools/autocode-schemas/continuous-planner-contract.schema.json so installed distributions do not need a repository checkout. The result must match the requested turn, requirements revision and producing route, and must report fresh. Validation failure preserves the previous usable draft.

ConversationStore in tools/dashboard/conversation_store.py routes existing intake documents to their original implementation. New continuous documents live in a separate directory and use independent Gatherer and Planner leases. Restart recovery commits validated captured results or retries only delivery known not to have started. An unknown provider outcome remains uncertain until there is authoritative evidence; a missing process does not authorize replay.

docs.title: Durable transfer to a task
docs.text:
autocode_conversation defines the version-1 handoff and runner journal. A handoff contains messages, unsent drafts, requirements history, structured plan history, configured routes, and available Gatherer/Planner dispatch receipts. Messages may include validated execution attribution (role, model, and optional engine, provider, reasoning_effort) plus a list of event_refs. These optional fields are absent from older handoffs, keeping their canonical digests unchanged. Dispatch receipts retain their original states and history.

The dashboard stages a digest-bound receipt inside the selected project's .autocode/conversation-handoffs/ directory and supplies its path using --conversation-handoff. The task accepts it under its run lock, verifies project ownership even when execution uses a child worktree, and writes conversation-journal.json. A repeated identical transfer is harmless; a different conversation or receipt cannot replace the journal. The single conversation_handoff state pointer records its ID, digest, staged path and journal path. The dashboard reads the journal after attachment.

Transferred drafts and receipts grant no approval. Attached product changes append conversation history and make the displayed draft stale; the runner's existing contract-change process controls replanning, review and reapproval.

docs.title: Explicit Build boundary
docs.text: Approval and Build are separate actions. After approval the dashboard sends --expected-goal-token with Build. Under the run lock, the CLI requires the same sealed approved contract, no unresolved questions, and the matching Architect final token for joint planning. It checks again before continuing. A successful Build request records one build_start user event for that token, distinct from goal_approval. A stale token does not launch a provider or record Build; retrying the same approved Build does not duplicate its event.

docs.title: Scoped model profile
docs.text:
The continuous profile applies only when creating a new task from a handoff. Ordinary CLI defaults and already saved task routes retain their configuration.

Role Model Reasoning Requirements Gatherer OpenAI GPT-6 Sol Low Planner, Builder and Builder retry OpenAI GPT-6 Sol High Resolver OpenAI GPT-6 Sol Max Plan Reviewer, Architect, Validator, Completion Owner Z.AI GLM 5.3 High Visual review OpenAI GPT-6 Astra High

Explicit incompatible routes are rejected before dispatch. The continuous profile keeps those routes during recovery: generic reasoning escalation does not change them, while the authorized Builder retry still runs on Sol High. The continuous profile disables default usage/time/idle/iteration caps; explicit CLI budgets remain authoritative. Verification and contract approval gates still apply.

Offline tests exercise the real adapter with a fake transport and the actual CLI with isolated temporary repositories. They do not claim an installed live-provider result or visual acceptance of the dashboard.

docs.title: Using the dashboard
docs.text:
Start a conversation without choosing a repository. The Requirements Gatherer responds in chat while the independent Planner updates the draft alongside it. On a narrow screen, the compact summary keeps the outstanding question visible; View plan opens the full draft without losing the conversation.

Choose a project when ready for repository-aware planning and Architect review. The same chat retains the original messages and draft history. When the exact plan is reviewed, Approve & build first records approval, waits for its confirmed receipt, then starts that approved revision. Build activity, validation, review findings, recovery and completion appear in the same conversation. The activity details retain each role's actual model and reasoning setting.

Sending a product change after approval invalidates the displayed plan gate. The existing task contract process must plan and review the change again before building it. A draft or ordinary chat message never grants approval.

If provider delivery is uncertain after a restart, the dashboard retains the message, draft and evidence. Retry is available only when saved evidence proves that delivery did not begin. Captured replies can be recovered without making another provider call.

docs.title: Live draft updates
docs.text:
The Requirements Gatherer replies to every human turn. Planner drafts are limited in two ways. The policy is in tools/dashboard/conversation_draft_cadence.py (schedule, launch, release):

  • Answer cadence. When no draft is running, an automatic update covers three answers (ANSWERS_PER_UPDATE). Between updates, the chat shows a Draft update card with Update draft now.
  • Coalescing. At most one Planner draft runs for each conversation. A turn that arrives while a draft is running does not start a Planner call. It is saved as a held intent (cadence_reason: coalesced_behind_draft_in_flight), and the card says the update will follow. When the running draft finishes, fails or is superseded before launch, at most one new draft starts. It is bound to the newest requirements revision, so it covers every turn that arrived meanwhile. The running draft's result is still discarded because newer input exists; the follow-up replaces it. A turn can arrive just after the running draft ends but before the follow-up starts; that turn's draft then becomes the follow-up. An explicit Update draft now request made while another draft is running joins that follow-up. Retry cannot force a second call. The chat composer stays open while a draft runs; only a Gatherer reply in flight or an uncertain Planner delivery holds it.
  • What counts as running. A draft counts from the moment it is queued for a worker in this dashboard until that worker ends, because the shared worker pool can hold it in a backlog first. It also counts while any worker holds its Planner delivery lease. The lease is an OS file lock, held in any dashboard process and released when that process exits. After a restart, recovery never replays a launched draft whose outcome is unknown. It starts the coalesced follow-up once nothing is running. If the draft ahead ended in another dashboard process, or died with it, opening the conversation starts the follow-up. A draft queued but not yet started in another dashboard process is not visible here: a turn sent then follows the answer cadence instead.
  • Stalled drafts. The Planner call has no timeout. A draft whose delivery record has not changed for STALLED_AFTER_SECONDS (10 minutes) stops blocking the follow-up: the card offers Update draft now again, and that request starts the follow-up at once. If the stalled call ever returns, its result is discarded as stale.

Any number of quick turns during one draft costs at most two Planner calls: the draft already running and one follow-up. Only an explicit update after a stall adds a call while the stalled one may still be running. If someone keeps answering faster than the Planner finishes, the dashboard makes at most one call per Planner run. The draft catches up once they pause.

Each draft records the human turns that caused it in freshness.source_messages. This covers every turn since the previous accepted draft, giving each turn's message ID, logical turn, requirements revision and a 240-character excerpt. The list is computed from the saved messages and requirements revisions when the draft opens, and it travels with the handoff. The draft card shows Updated after your answers: "…" · "…" with a short quote for each turn, instead of the generic freshness label. A coalesced draft lists all of its turns. Only a draft the Planner produced (freshness.structured_result) shows causes; a pending, failed or superseded placeholder claims no update. Drafts never grant approval.

docs.title: History and permanent deletion
docs.text:
Archive keeps files and is reversible. A temporary workspace confirmed missing by fresh filesystem and worker checks moves into history and returns if it reappears. Unavailable or uncertain status does not qualify for automatic cleanup.

Permanent deletion is a separate explicit action. Preview names the selected run and exact paths. Removing a dedicated task worktree or branch is optional and available only after exclusive ownership is verified. Confirmation is bound to the inspected contents and refuses running or uncertain tasks, symbolic links, changed paths and shared workspaces. If a step fails, the receipt shows what remains and permits retry of that same confirmed deletion. Files recreated after a completed deletion require a new preview.

docs.title: Measuring the cost of issue solving
Every task, continuously
docs.text:
Each run keeps its token and cost totals current while it works. Nothing needs to be switched on and no model is called.

  • Status view. usage in the view (autocode --run-dir RUN --status, Task run) holds the run's totals so far: stages, tokens, cost_usd (reported, estimated, complete), unknown_stages and the same by role. cost holds the spend at current list prices against the run's money cap, and --status prints it as one Cost: ... line on stderr (below). escalations prices each escalation's attempts the same way and says how it ended, so a run shows what each climb cost and whether it helped (status view).
  • Project ledger. PROJECT/.autocode/usage.jsonl has one row per run, rewritten at every checkpoint save, so it is right during a task and after it pauses, completes or is killed. It is under .autocode/, which Git ignores.
  • Report. python3 tools/autocode_usage.py [PROJECT] prints one line per run and a total; --json prints the rows.

Cost has three bases, always kept apart: reported is the provider's own cost_usd (the built-in claude provider writes each call's share of Claude Code's cumulative session cost; a provider that reports none, or only a zero for a subscription plan, has none); estimated is tokens at the frozen comparison rates in autocode_usage.REFERENCE_PRICES, and only for the models listed there (today GLM-5.3 on the Z.AI coding plan and MiMo v2.6 Pro on the Xiaomi token plan); anything else is unknown, not zero. complete is false while a stage has no cost or is still running, so a total is then a floor. Stages the runner executes itself (the regression proof, the orchestrator) cost nothing. Any other model, such as an OpenAI route, has no comparison estimate until a rate is added there; the status view's cost field prices it from the dated table below instead.

Parallel Builders are counted once, in their parent. A worker run keeps no ledger of its own: when a batch finishes, the parent copies each worker's finished stages, cost included, into its own record (autocode_dispatch.account_workers), so the parent's row holds them. While a batch is still running its workers' spend is not yet in the parent's row; it appears when the batch is accounted.

docs.title: Current prices and the money cap
docs.text:
tools/autocode_prices.json is the dated price table: per model, the input, output and (where published) cached-input price in USD per million tokens, the provider page it was read from and the date. Rows change by pull request; autocode models --prices prints it with the rate each default route is priced at, or "no rate". A bare model id (the Codex engine's) is priced as openai/<id>, and an OpenCode 2.x #effort suffix is ignored. A subscription or coding-plan route's row is the metered API price of the same model, so its spend is an API-equivalent figure, not the plan's bill.

A row keeps the rates it replaced in history, each with until, the UTC date from which it no longer applies. A stage is priced at the rate in force on the UTC day it finished, so a tariff update never rewrites what an earlier stage cost or whether a resumed run is over its cap. Change a rate by moving the old one into history with until set to the new rate's first day; editing a rate in place reprices every earlier stage. A stage with no finish time is priced at today's rate.

The status view's cost field and the Cost: ... line use this table: each finished stage counts its reported cost, else its tokens at the table's rates (cache reads at the cached rate when their count is known), else it is unpriced and not counted. The money cap (--max-cost-usd, Money cap) compares that spend at every stage boundary. The frozen comparison rates above stay separate: evidence reports and campaign comparisons are bound to them, so a price update never changes a published report's binding. That is why usage.cost_usd.estimated and cost.estimated_usd can differ.

docs.title: Outcome-linked status
docs.text:
The public status view also exposes usage.accounting and efficiency. These are additive measurement projections, not new acceptance gates or model calls.

  • Accounting keeps individual failed, interrupted, active and report-repair attempts. Native requests are deduplicated by session and part identity. Missing finishes, conflicting duplicates and absent token components remain explicitly incomplete; a known subtotal is not a complete total, even when another component is priced.
  • Observed execution intervals, summed execution durations and provider-request intervals are separate. Parallel overlap is not added to wall time twice. Unobserved waiting, setup or visual-inspection time is not inferred from gaps. Time waiting for the person is measured from each request a person answered: from when it became answerable to their response (efficiency.time, category waiting). A request superseded or still pending adds nothing. OpenCode request starts are paired within the same session and message. Multiple pending starts for one message leave its timing unknown and coverage explicitly uncertain; known finish-token receipts are retained. Message-free events use legacy FIFO only in entirely message-free sessions, and cannot consume another message's start. Conflicting message bindings in a replay invalidate timing for both affected messages without duplicating usage.
  • Runner check observations distinguish execution, repeated execution, reuse and suppression, with reasons and original receipt provenance. A required independent or canonical execution is not classified as wasted merely because it repeats a command. Recovery after a checkpoint crash imports a retained check's original duration once; reusing that receipt does not execute or charge those seconds again.
  • autocode_efficiency.aggregate consumes supplied public task-run views, not other runs' private state. It keeps root deliveries distinct from worker completions, deduplicates imported request identities, and reports missing worker coverage.
  • Accepted-task unit metrics require the current checkout's full completion gate, not just a historical TASK_COMPLETE. A stale checkout contributes no current delivery; a state-only view without a fresh gate result keeps acceptance unknown. Unit metrics remain undefined without an accepted root outcome or complete usage. unit_metrics.reported_usd divides only provider-reported cost; unit_metrics.spent_usd divides the status view's cost.spent_usd (reported, else the dated-table estimate), so a coding-plan run gets a figure too, and only while cost.complete is true. Experiment reports must additionally apply their external delivery oracle; the status projection cannot establish untested product quality.

Visual acceptance remains a separate, stronger requirement. A manifest case, produced screenshot, model assertion or green functional suite does not establish that an independent reviewer inspected the reference and current candidate images. Until the runner supplies authoritative current-bound visual acceptance receipts, accepted-frame/state counts, first-acceptance times and visual unit costs are null with an explanation. Do not substitute zero, count mapped criteria as accepted screens, or advertise visual savings from a generic TASK_COMPLETE.

Failed ledger writes emit a visible warning without changing the task outcome. That warning is a measurement gap, not evidence that the missing usage was free.

The sections below describe the scorer and sampler, which inspect a saved run after the fact.

The existing scorer and live sampler can inspect a saved run without launching providers or changing its state:

python3 tools/score_autocode_run.py --run-dir /path/to/run \
  --out /tmp/run-score.md --json-out /tmp/run-score.json
python3 tools/live_token_sampler.py --run-dir /path/to/run \
  --json-out /tmp/run-steps.json

Both also work as Python modules (python3 -m tools.score_autocode_run and python3 -m tools.live_token_sampler) from the repository root.

docs.title: How to interpret the numbers
docs.text:
The scorer's token_usage.estimated_api_equivalent_usd uses the existing historical comparison rates, recorded in pricing_basis. These are not verified current prices or actual charges. The calculation prices inclusive input and output once at flat rates, without a cache discount. Subscription fees, exhausted quotas, and human time require separate accounting.

  • Runner-normalized input already includes cached tokens; output includes reasoning. The scorer does not add either subset again.
  • Raw OpenCode steps report separate input, cache reads, cache writes, visible output, and reasoning. All five buckets contribute once.
  • Unknown models have no fallback price. Missing or invalid usage is unknown, not zero. Explicit zero remains zero.
  • A missing cost in any recorded stage makes the complete estimate null. known_estimated_api_equivalent_usd remains available as a subtotal, with unpriced_stages reporting its coverage gap. An active stage also prevents a complete estimate, even if it has partial usage.
  • Failed, timed-out, and abandoned stages remain in the accounting. A valid runner-owned transition has no inference cost.
  • Historical models come from the saved launch command, falling back to a model explicitly saved on the attempt. Today's role configuration cannot establish which model ran yesterday.

The sampler reads only event paths recorded in that run's state and located inside its directory. It ignores unregistered copies and deduplicates repeated updates by session and part ID within each log. Records without IDs cannot be deduplicated reliably. Conflicting model identities for one log remain unknown. Only OpenCode step events are sampled; normalized provider usage still appears in the scorer's stage table for other transports.

Sampler totals always describe observed steps only. They do not establish complete coverage: a crashed request, missing log, or unfinished call may consume additional tokens. Do not add step totals to stage totals; they describe overlapping usage. JSON consumers must accept nullable counts and estimates. The sampler now exposes models per stage because retries can change models.

docs.title: Evaluation milestone
docs.text:
Use this accounting to establish a baseline before changing orchestration or model selection. The next issue-evaluation work should record:

  1. A frozen repository revision, issue requirements, and reproducible setup.
  2. Every attempt, including setup and provider failures, with stable identities.
  3. Independent candidate-bound checks and patch review; a runner completion claim or this scorer's heuristic dimension scores are not an acceptance oracle.
  4. Assisted versus unassisted delivery, elapsed time, and human intervention time.
  5. Total campaign cost divided by independently verified fixes, including failed attempts in the numerator. With missing cost data, publish a known subtotal and coverage gap instead of a complete cost-per-fix claim.

Start with a small development set and keep separate held-out issues. Compare against a single-agent baseline with the same models, tools, and budget. Expand only after the common failure causes are understood. This baseline and model effectiveness comparison have not yet been established by the accounting tests.

docs.title: Regression checks
docs.text:
.venv/bin/python -m unittest tests.test_cost_reporting tests.test_efficiency \
  tests.test_usage tests.test_autocode_request_usage tests.test_opencode tests.test_opencode_length \
  tests.test_prices tests.test_cost tests.test_cost_cap -q

These checks use synthetic provider events and local fixture executables. They cover cost arithmetic against the actual provider normalizer, missing data, retry model identity, repeated events, failed attempts, and both CLI entry paths. They make no live model calls. The subprocess fixture needs local process-table access for its process-supervision checks.

docs.title: Where a run spent money
docs.text: cost.breakdown in --status --json attributes the money-cap ledger by stage and process outcome. Repeated stages and failed/interrupted attempts also appear in the Cost: line, with their known subtotal and unpriced count. Reported and estimated amounts stay separate in JSON. A process that exits successfully may still reject a plan; a failed check can be useful. This breakdown measures where money went, without labelling those attempts productive or wasted. Restored checkpoint spend remains separately identified as inherited_usd. See the status contract for completeness and rounding semantics.

docs.title: Browser dashboard
docs.text:
← Back to README

Autocode includes a local browser dashboard for planning work with the Requirements Planner, approving the lead-reviewed plan, choosing each execution role's model and reasoning level, following active tasks, and sending feedback or a pause request at a safe boundary. It reads the same local run registry as the command line tool, so tasks started from a terminal appear automatically.

docs.title: Start it
docs.text:
After installing this checkout, start it from any directory:

autocode-dashboard --port 8767

Or run it directly from a checkout:

python3 tools/dashboard/agent_console.py --port 8767

Open the printed loopback URL. Projects contain multiple conversations. Use a project’s + button to start a conversation scoped to its repository and instructions. The top New conversation action names its current project. Conversations without a project remain in No project, and can be attached explicitly when ready.

Workspace setup opens a chat with dependency checks, model settings and project creation. It never collects credentials or runs installers. New projects receive an empty initial Git commit; attaching an existing project requires a clean committed repository. Older scoped chats without a saved folder identity ask you to confirm the displayed folder in chat. Confirmation preserves history and starts no model work. A known replacement folder remains blocked until the original is restored.

When --watch-root is used, discovery stops at each Git project boundary and skips generated or internal trees such as .git, .autocode, node_modules, and virtual environments. List responses also keep only the compact stage data needed by the task index, so broad workspace roots remain safe to poll from the browser without serializing complete provider payloads or process histories. Overlapping task-index polls share the same in-progress snapshot, and each snapshot reuses one watched-project discovery result instead of building a queue of duplicate scans.

docs.title: Preview and saved screenshots
docs.text:
While autocode serve start runs a run's development server (Development server), Preview shows that server with no address to enter. It notes whether the server was started on the run's latest saved step, reloads the frame when the server restarts after a code change, and waits while the server starts instead of switching to another app. When the server is not running, Preview says why (stopped, exited with its exit code, or no longer answering), says when it starts again after the next code change, or shows the autocode serve start command to run from a terminal.

Otherwise Preview shows the loopback app address you saved for the project in this browser; it is also the fallback while the run's server is not running. Open Preview from any conversation in that project to reuse it. Existing task-level addresses remain available. The dashboard starts no development server itself. A completed code-changing step refreshes the preview; ordinary status polling preserves the running frame.

A Validator image reference appears in chat beside its requirement and recorded source revision. Open the image or follow its link to Checks. These are saved results, not new visual acceptance. When a recorded image fingerprint exists, the dashboard refuses changed bytes. Missing images, unsupported formats, stale report IDs, symlinks and paths outside the selected task/project are refused. No image card approves a requirement or starts a task.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
The conversation contains questions, exact-plan approval, output acceptance and recovery actions. Approving a reviewed plan and starting its build are separate actions. An amber marker beside a conversation means it requires your reply; opening it does not dismiss the request. A completed conversation shows a tick.

Archive and Remove project change visibility and preserve files and checkpoints. Delete permanently is a separate explicit action in Archived. Its confirmation dialog lists the selected files and owned Git resources. Live or uncertain workers, changed selections and shared resources prevent deletion. Partial cleanup retains a retry receipt and never treats a recreated resource as owned.

Saved code checkpoints offer comparison and Go back to here in chat. An approved restore requires a stopped run and creates a new branch and paused continuation. It preserves the previous branch and history; later verification does not carry over as proof for the restored version.

Choose initial reasoning under Models & reasoning when starting a conversation. For a saved task, open its ••• menu and use Reasoning for next steps. The dashboard changes the saved per-role setting only at a stage boundary; it never interrupts or mutates an in-flight provider request.

The dashboard uses $AUTOCODE_HOME/dashboard by default (or $AUTOCODE_DASHBOARD_HOME) for conversations and reversible archive settings. It binds only to 127.0.0.1, starts no development server for task previews, and uses documented Autocode commands for task changes.

docs.title: Conversation and artifact panes
docs.text:
Chat stays visible throughout planning, building, verification and recovery. The Work pane shows the current task, recorded roles, factual task progress, requirements and blockers. Plan, Preview, Changes, Checks and History open beside it without replacing the conversation. On narrow screens, Projects and Details open as drawers and preserve the chat draft. Workspace options contains All work, Archived and display preferences.

Pause and Stop beside the composer finish the current step before preventing further stages. Their pending labels do not claim the runner has stopped yet. Compact task links and older #task=…&run=… links remain supported.

Saved status, worker liveness, artifact timestamps, and task-read freshness are separate signals. A disconnected task retains its last successful view, labels it stale, disables mutations, and offers Retry status. Refreshing the project list does not make a failed task read look current. HTTP read failures never resume, restart, or retry an agent stage.

An open task also carries the run's public status view (status_view, from the same cached autocode --status call that fills the intervention panel), so detail panes read fields such as changes_by_criterion, dev_server and needs from the contract in docs/task-run.md. It is null when that call fails. The project list still reads saved run state for fields the view does not carry; that read is confined to dashboard_run_state.py, and the dashboard uses only public names of core modules (both checked in tests/test_architecture.py).

In Checks, each requirement's Inspect section lists, beside its recorded evidence, the saved Builder steps of the milestones that cover it and each file's diff against the saved step before it (GET /api/criterion-diffs, which calls autocode_review_diff.criterion_diffs on that same status view and reads committed Git objects, never the working tree). The changes are labelled as attribution, not proof that the requirement is met. A requirement whose steps also changed files another requirement's milestone changed is marked as overlapping. Parallel Builders' integrated work is one saved step that served several milestones; it is headed with all of them (milestones B, C), and each requirement shows only its own milestone's files of it, naming the files it leaves out ("Not shown, changed in this step for another milestone"). When a requirement has no attributed step, or the run's status is unavailable, it says so and offers View all run changes, which opens Changes. The pane is read once per run until a step is saved or its attribution changes.

docs.title: Project-specific counters
docs.text:
Project-specific counters are optional. Declare a read-only projection in the project's .autocode/dashboard.json (not in runner state):

{
  "version": 1,
  "metrics": [{
    "id": "mapping", "label": "Mapping coverage", "runs": ["EXACT-RUN-DIRECTORY-NAME"],
    "description": "Dispositioned records, not completion or mastery.",
    "source": "artifacts/coverage.json", "groups_pointer": "/areas",
    "completed_field": "done", "total_field": "total"
  }]
}

The referenced object contains named groups, each with integer counters or lists whose lengths are counted. Sources must remain inside that project (including after symlink resolution). Invalid/missing data is unavailable, never zero or PASS. The artifact modification time is shown prominently. A cached projection avoids repeatedly parsing large files; changes to the file or config invalidate it. No commands, imports, provider requests, or raw content are executed by these metric declarations. Removing the config removes the panel. An exact run-name allowlist prevents another task inheriting unrelated progress.

docs.title: Dashboard verification
docs.text:
With localhost socket access:

python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/dashboard/tests -p 'test_*.py'
for test_file in tools/dashboard/tests/test_*.js; do node "$test_file" || exit 1; done
python3 tools/dashboard/tests/unified_browser_fixture.py

CI runs the Python suite and the Node tests on macOS and Linux, except test_m3_lifecycle_browser_ui.js and test_shell_a11y_ui.js, which drive the agent-browser CLI and need it installed.

The browser fixture uses disposable workspaces and cannot launch agents. The exception is the chat client's acceptance test, test_scenario_client_browser_ui.js: it types the parallel-diamond scenario's brief in chat, attaches a project, approves and builds the plan, and checks each requirement's changes against the scenario's reference solution at three viewport sizes. Its fixture runs the real runner on the fake OpenCode client, which hands each stage to the scenario harness's scripted model, so no model is called. The packaged-import regression tests the installed entry-point layout, not just the source-directory import path. Updating files does not reload a running dashboard: restart only its server at an idle boundary, preserving the same environment and storage paths. Do not interrupt queued dashboard actions or provider requests. The autonomous runner is independent and does not need restarting.

docs.title: macOS app
docs.text:
macos-app/ contains a native macOS app that hosts the same dashboard in its own window. See macOS app.

See also: Registry API · Interventions · Models

docs.title: Build and publish the documentation
docs.text:
The site renders the existing docs/ Markdown files with Material for MkDocs. The front page and README name the same five first-day guides. Historical bug notes and design plans stay in the repository and remain linked from the guides. They are not copied into a second documentation tree.

Use a separate environment for documentation tooling:

python3 -m venv .docs-venv
source .docs-venv/bin/activate
pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
mkdocs build --strict
mkdocs serve

The strict build is the CI link check: missing local targets and internal anchors fail it. Source links that leave the published guide set are checked against the checkout and rendered as GitHub links at the exact built revision. Code examples are not rewritten. This checks repository cross-references; it does not promise that every third-party URL is available.

docs/site_hooks.py generates the stage table from tools/autocode_roles.py and rewrites source links. To change a role name, edit the canonical module rather than the generated table. No generated HTML belongs in master.

docs.title: Publication
docs.text:
The documentation workflow builds every pull request. Only a push to master or a v* release tag can publish. The publication job uses the GitHub Pages artifact deployment with explicit contents, pages and OIDC permissions. GitHub Pages must use GitHub Actions as its publishing source. In the github-pages environment, allow deployments from the master branch and v* tags; Pages initially permits only the default branch.

Mike stores generated versions in gh-pages. Master updates only latest and the site's root redirect. A release tag adds its own version and preserves latest and all earlier versions. Older master workflow reruns skip publication. Publication is serialized so these updates do not overwrite each other. The release-tag hook is ready for the first versioned release; creating a documentation site does not create or publish a package release.

For a local versioning rehearsal, use a disposable clone and local branch:

mike deploy --branch docs-preview --ignore-remote-status latest
mike set-default --branch docs-preview --ignore-remote-status latest
mike deploy --branch docs-preview --ignore-remote-status v0.0.0-test
mike list --branch docs-preview

This writes only the disposable clone. It does not push or deploy to Pages.

docs.title: Exact output transport
docs.text:
AutoCode can shorten verified passing unittest output while retaining every failure, diagnostic and original byte. New runs use --tool-output-mode conservative; use --tool-output-mode raw to display everything. This policy applies to AutoCode's capture and output commands. Native provider tools are not intercepted, and their permissions stay unchanged.

autocode "Fix the parser" --workspace /path/to/project --tool-output-mode raw

Saved runs retain their policy. Runs created before this setting use raw mode. Change a saved policy only at a reconciled pause, with --resume-paused --tool-output-mode raw (or conservative). An active or uncertain attempt must be reconciled first. A single capture can always request raw output with --no-compress.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Run these inside the target project. Every capture needs a unique receipt name:

autocode capture --output .autocode/evidence/tests-001.json -- python -m unittest -v
autocode capture --no-compress --output .autocode/evidence/tests-002.json -- python -m unittest -v
autocode output read src/parser.py --start-line 40 --end-line 90
autocode output read src/parser.py --known-sha256 FULL_FILE_SHA256
autocode output retrieve FULL_FILE_SHA256 --raw --start-line 40 --end-line 90
autocode output retrieve FULL_FILE_SHA256 --raw
autocode output status

Only python[version] -m unittest ... with a recognized completion footer and matching exit status is filtered. Repeated diagnostics stay verbatim. Unknown commands, incomplete runs and unrecognized output stay raw. The displayed omission markers identify original line ranges. JSON is kept as original text; binary output is base64 encoded in JSON and retrievable as exact bytes.

output read returns exact lines, full-file SHA-256, original byte length and omitted ranges. Conservative reads default to 200 lines; raw mode returns the whole file unless an explicit range is requested. The complete original is retained before any omission. --known-sha256 is an explicit assertion that the caller already knows that exact file identity; it is not a conversation cache inferred by AutoCode. An unchanged result includes a retrieval command. A changed file returns its new content and identity. Its earlier version stays retrievable, even after the file is deleted or a process restarts.

capture --known-output-sha256 HASH can omit an identical display after exact retrieval is verified. It still executes the command, returns its fresh exit status and creates a fresh receipt. References, shortened displays and earlier PASS results never substitute for current verification or independent acceptance.

docs.title: Recovery and retained data
docs.text:
The full command log remains beside its receipt. Exact copies live in .autocode/output/blobs, named by their full SHA-256. Existing artifacts are never overwritten or evicted automatically. Partial writes cannot become valid retained artifacts. Corrupt or unavailable storage makes a read/capture fall back to complete output; retrieving corrupt bytes fails explicitly. A killed capture leaves its partial log without a completion receipt and refuses reuse of that filename. Use a fresh name for a new execution.
