Field Meaning version 1 path "compact" (the runner wrote the draft; the Plan Reviewer reviews it) or "full" (the Planner's draft runs) reasons Every trusted signal that kept the full path, in words (the run did not opt in (--compact-bugfix-planning), the project declares no sensitive-paths, so every path counts as sensitive, the fix touches sensitive paths: ..., the compact draft was refused: ...); [] on the compact path basis The records the decision rests on: diagnosis_output_hash, diagnosis_source_revision and requirements_output decisions One row for astra_discovery (the Planner's draft): decision is "omitted" or "included", with its reason, and covered_by names what covers an omission (runner:compact_draft, astra_challenge, person:approve_goal, runner:regression_proof) fallback null, or {"from": "astra_challenge", "reason": ..., "review_call_refunded": true/false} once a review could not approve the compact draft and the run returned to the full path (the compact review's call is given back to the full path's allowance)

The record reports a decision the core made from trusted inputs; it grants nothing, and a client renders it without acting on it.

proxied_requirements lists the requirements the current plan proves only on a stand-in (#2068): the user-visible result is rendered by code outside this checkout, so the plan's criteria prove an internal value the result is believed to depend on. Each row has requirement_id, evidence (the criteria it cites) and proxy_reason. A plan may mark a requirement proxied only with the person's word: a saved answer cited in proxy_reason, or until then a blocking decision question about that requirement, which the run asks before the plan can be approved. It is [] when there are none or no plan yet, and it grants nothing; the approval screen lists the same rows under "Proven only on a stand-in".

needs is null when the run is complete. Otherwise its kind says what the run is waiting for:

kind Waiting for Extra fields Answer with approve_plan approval of the plan AutoCode displayed token Approve the plan answer answers to clarifying questions or a decision questions (id, question, why, options, proposed_default), request_kind; for a question Resolver published, also resolver_request_id, resolver_token and resolver_scope; with resolver_scope blocker or operational_exhaustion (and no route), action is the response command; when pause_origin is PAUSED_NO_PROGRESS because a repeated incident was held, also retry_action (--resume-paused --retry-failed-stage), the one scoped retry the hold admits after inspection Answer, with the current resolver_token; the questions left return under a new one. A question with options takes exactly one of those labels or its proposed_default; free text answers only a question without options. A blocker or operational_exhaustion request refuses --answer and takes action (respond_operational()), or, after inspection, retry_action (retry_failed_stage()) review a person to accept specific acceptance criteria criteria, token, question Approve a review, per criterion planning_budget more plan-review calls reason Plan feedback, or --planning-review-call-limit N recover_source an attempt without a saved original source identity retained retry metadata, recovery_hint; action is null Inspect the archive and current changes before a new run retry_job inspection of a stopped workflow job job_retry_token, archive, write_diagnosis, recovery_hint; route after quota, a content-filter refusal, an authenticated output limit, authentication failure or a fully stopped execution timeout Exact retry after restoring original source; with route, name another model first resume a person to inspect a pause and resolve its cause reason; new_run_required with action=fresh_run preserves an immutable caller-binding failure and requires a new run; edit_required at a repairable component-plan stop prescribes action (--edit-goal FILE) or feedback_action (--feedback TEXT), then fresh approval; at PAUSED_ACCEPTANCE_TESTS (the Tester's pause) action is --feedback 'WHAT TO CHANGE', which revises the plan and returns the run to plan approval, chat.input offers the same feedback message, and guidance says that --resume-paused reruns the Tester unchanged and helps only once the code changed; otherwise action when one command continues, such as --resume-paused --no-progress-limit N at a PAUSED_NO_PROGRESS its unchanged-batch limit caused, with no_progress_batches, the retained count N must exceed (or N is 0), or --resume-paused --retry-builder M at a parallel Builder member's quota, content-filter or output-limit stop whose request was answered without a model, or --resume-paused --retry-failed-stage (also as retry_action) at a recovery novelty hold whose request is not yet published, where a plain resume would hold again; when that hold cannot take the retry yet, retry_unavailable instead says why (an owned or uncertain attempt to reconcile, or a different pending decision), the same reason the CLI gives; an attempt that exited cleanly with a recorded finish (a verification hold or stale source check stands on its result) keeps abandon_stage and its --abandon-stage ATTEMPT then --resume-paused action as a resume, because archiving it would discard that result; at a PAUSED_REPEATED_FAILURE whose active attempt, uncertain artifacts or pending report repair its retry gate will not authorize over, retry_unavailable carries that CLI refusal verbatim and action is the plain --resume-paused, never the rejected --retry-failed-stage (#1897) Start a fresh run when required; otherwise correct and freshly approve an edit-required plan, or resume once resolved dependency a bound producer run's delivery (see Dependencies between existing runs) reason, producer_run, producer_workspace autocode wait --run-dir <producer_run> --workspace <producer_workspace>: returns when the producer needs a person or ends. Nothing to answer on this run: the dependency worker (python tools/autocode_dependencies.py ... --watch) calls --receive-dependency MANIFEST (TaskRun.receive_dependency) when the producer's verified delivery is ready continue no person input; the core may name a deterministic recovery in action (for example, setting aside an uncertain attempt that did not finish cleanly, or resuming bounded recovery when the saved progress ledger proves another slot is unnecessary) action when present Run only the named next_command, then read status again

A resolver_scope of operational_exhaustion or blocker means Resolver stopped the run because it could not continue safely (for example, the run time limit was reached). That question is for a person who has looked at the run; a caller must not answer it with a proposed default. Its action is the response command. A blocker is often a decision about the approved contract (a criterion Resolver proved contradictory): the response is retained as information and never edits the contract, so after it the run holds and needs.reason names the path that applies such a decision, --edit-goal body.json followed by --approve-goal.

When a role's quota ran out, its provider's content filter refused it, or its authenticated response exhausted the output limit, the answer need also carries route: question_id (route-ROLE), role, job, current_model, engine, cause (quota, content_filter or output_limit), stopped_model and, for a refusal, candidates (configured models that would pass the launch rules; advice only). Its question has no default and is never delegable; only a model a person names answers it (--answer route-ROLE=MODEL), and the run then needs a resume. A stopped workflow job carries the same route, with the same fields, on its retry_job need (Failed workflow jobs).

When a person named a role's reasoning effort and the role's model does not declare that level (GLM 5.3 declares low, high and max, not medium), the run pauses as PAUSED_EFFORT_UNSUPPORTED before any stage launches (#2057). Its answer need carries effort: question_id (effort-ROLE), role, job, model, requested, declared (the levels the model offers) and nearest (the declared level nearest the requested one; advice, never a default). Its one question lists declared as its options, has no proposed_default and is never delegable. next_command is --answer effort-ROLE=EFFORT with no token: a client fills EFFORT with one of declared a person chose, and refuses anything else. The answer saves that level as the person's own choice and launches nothing; the run then needs a resume. An effort the runner chose is never asked about: the launch moves it to the nearest declared level and records the move.

Approving a plan or a review is a real user decision. Automated callers should do it only when a person has delegated that decision to them, as the scenario harness does for test runs.

Resolver scopes preserve separate decision authority even when they share a needs kind. The fast execution matrix in tests/test_needs_execution_matrix.py checks these scopes through the CLI's saved-action pipeline and the public TaskRun methods; adding a scope or a needs-table row requires an execution case.

Resolver scope Need and decision Authority retained after the decision clarification answer: answer with the displayed Resolver token Intent is saved for fresh planning; execution is not approved goal_approval approve_plan: approve the displayed sealed plan token Only that current plan gains approval permission answer: select an offered scoped permission answer The existing approved contract is preserved goal_change answer: answer the proposed change with its current token Fresh planning and approval remain necessary human_review review: accept a named criterion with its current artifact token Source and technical-evidence pins must still match blocker answer: use respond_operational, not an ordinary answer Corrective information does not edit the contract or authorize execution operational_exhaustion answer: use respond_operational, not an ordinary answer Existing limits hold; information is considered at the next explicit resume intake answer: answer the Resolver intake question with its current token Intent is saved; no project plan or execution approval is implied

AutoResolver never changes the approved contract itself. The resolver policy defines a replan action (autocode_resolver.ACTIONS), but every decision the runner asks of it admits only continue, retry and escalate, and a diagnosis only retry and escalate. A contract change always goes through fresh planning and the person's approval of the new plan token. This is deliberate: the Resolver adapter does not authorize contract replanning, implementation replay, new permissions or completion.

docs.title: Supervision timing in status
docs.text: view.liveness.timing reports an authenticated supervision receipt's monotonic_elapsed_seconds, wall_elapsed_seconds, admitted_stage_limit_seconds, excess_wall_seconds, suspension_tolerance_seconds and likely_host_or_vm_suspension. Legacy or malformed timing is null. A runner check exposes the same evidence at view.runner_check.liveness.timing. This is passive evidence: stage, idle and tool limits and supervision triggers continue to use monotonic awake time only.

docs.title: Runner checks in status
docs.text:
view.runner_check describes a local check in progress before the Tester: its stage, plain-language summary, started_at, updated_at, command and output path. It is null when no such check is active. These checks do not consume a model turn. A resumed run saves its running state before the first test starts, so it does not continue to look paused throughout a long suite.

The CLI also returns runner_check_workers with checked, alive and live_pids, using the controller's recorded process birth identity. An exited controller makes the checkpoint stale; an inaccessible process is unknown, not assumed dead. Inspect retained test output before restarting a stale check. The check activity never substitutes for a passing proof or independent review.

docs.title: Work in another repository
docs.text:
view.scope reports work the request places in another repository (#2066). Requirements names each part, and the runner keeps it only when its quote is verbatim in the request or a saved answer, or when it cites a file in this workspace that shows it.

  • spans_repositories and external_parts (target, work) list the kept parts.
  • dropped names the targets of the parts the runner refused.
  • decision is this_repository once the person chose it, else null.
  • uncovered lists the targets this run leaves out.
  • linked lists the other runs of this run's change set: the source run and each run linked to it (changeset, target, role source or member, workspace, run_dir, which is null while a linked run is starting). It is [] for a run in no change set.
  • briefs holds a ready brief (repository, brief) for each repository the request spans, this one first, for a person who stops here and runs them separately.

A kept part stops the run before any plan, with one nondelegable question (workspace-scope-<identity>, kind answer). The question binds the current human turn and feedback to the exact external work; clients use its offered ID. The same gate applies to a reproduced Investigator diagnosis and a follow-up with an existing goal. Its only option is This repository only. Other text is refused, and --feedback TEXT changes the request instead. After that answer the plan must record each uncovered part in scope_exclusions as Not covered: changes in TARGET: WORK, and displayed_plan.scope_exclusions shows it on the approval screen. The Planner's packet names the exact entries (scope_exclusions_required). A saved answer may correct one authenticated boundary's exact wording: a user-backed reworded declaration whose replacement still names the same peer moves that entry to the corrected text in every later draft and packet, while the scope and assignment it was recorded under stay the same; a removal, a moved boundary or an unbacked declaration keeps the original entry (#2467).

docs.title: Linked runs
docs.text:
autocode changeset link --run-dir RUN --target TARGET --workspace PROJECT [--json] [-- OPTIONS] starts a run in another repository for one of the source run's scope.external_parts. It is a layer above this interface: it reads the source run's status view and starts the linked run with TaskRun.start, nothing else.

  • TARGET must be a target in the source run's scope.external_parts.
  • PROJECT must be an available project in the AutoCode registry (autocode registry list), named by its path or registry id. A path from the task text or a model's report is never used. An operator can register a fresh committed local checkout with autocode registry add PATH, without starting a task. Linking runs directly in that selected checkout; choose a dedicated Git worktree if needed.
  • The linked run's brief is the source run's scope.briefs entry for TARGET. Arguments after -- are the linked run's run options, such as its engine and models.
  • The link is recorded in changesets.json beside the registry, so both commands need the same AUTOCODE_HOME. A target is linked once. A link whose run never started is dropped, so it can be made again. Linking from an existing member extends its canonical set, preserving the original source. The same target or workspace cannot be added twice. Ambiguous overlapping records from older versions are refused rather than choosing a different set for status and inventory.
  • autocode changeset status --run-dir RUN [--json] shows the change set of any of its runs, each with the status, needs kind and next_command of its own status view. autocode changeset list [--json] lists every change set.

Linking does not answer the source run's scope question: its plan still records the linked target as not covered there. Adding a member withdraws any shared execution release, so the enlarged set needs a fresh approval of all current plans.

docs.title: Approving the set
docs.text:
changeset status shows each run's plan (runs[].plan, the complete displayed_plan its token approves) and approval:

  • set_token is a digest of every run's identity and own plan token. It is null until every run offers a complete plan for approval, including a previously approved plan still held after an interrupted set approval. waiting_on names runs without an offer.
  • next_command is the argument array that approves the set, or null. It is also null when every run has already completed under its approved plan: an unchanged completed run joins a revised set with that plan, but a set with no new plan has nothing to approve.

autocode changeset approve --run-dir RUN --set-token TOKEN reads every run's view again. It refuses a token that no longer matches, then records a durable hold for the exact membership before approving any member. Each approval uses the public TaskRun.approve_plan(plan_token, changeset_token=set_token) operation, transported as --approve-goal - --changeset-token - with AUTOCODE_APPROVE_GOAL_TOKEN and AUTOCODE_CHANGESET_TOKEN. Each core publishes only its own exact approval at its durable checkpoint; the coordinator never reads another run's private state.

The shared release is committed only after every member checkpoint has accepted the same set. A failed/interrupted approval leaves all members held; inspect the current plans and repeat the offered set approval to finish it. A later plan, task turn or membership change withdraws the release before that changed checkpoint can commit. The core checks the receipt before execution, including resumed and parallel Builder work; an already dispatched attempt retains its normal safe-boundary lifecycle.

An explicit individual --approve-goal remains available and releases only that exact run plan and turn. Reapproval after a held set uses the ordinary AutoResolver plan request boundary and cannot clear a different pause, pending question or uncertain attempt. An ordinary resume cannot release a held set. changeset status.record_revision is the monotonic coordination-record revision used to reject stale record mutations.

docs.title: Checking the set together and delivering it
docs.text:
Each run still passes its own completion gate. changeset status adds verification:

  • waiting_on lists the runs not yet TASK_COMPLETE. Nothing is checked together before then.
  • check is the integration command the person named, result its last run and waiver the person's reason to accept the set without it. A result or waiver carries check_identity and current. It is current only while the named command and execution target, member run/workspace identities, every run's status and every workspace's code (commit, diff and untracked files, AutoCode's own excluded) match the recorded evidence. Historical results and waivers without the check identity remain readable but are not current; run the check again or record a fresh explicit waiver rather than inferring approval for an unknown command.
  • done is true once every run is complete and either no command was named, a current result passed, or a current waiver exists.
  • merge_order and next_command (the verify argument array, while a check is due).

The summary's additive record_revision identifies the inspected change-set record. Changing the check, verifying and waiving use a conditional write against that revision. If a command, membership, waiver or competing check result changes the record while verification runs, its old result cannot overwrite the new record or certify a replacement command. The action refuses and asks for fresh inspection.

The actions:

  • changeset check-command --run-dir RUN --in TARGET -- COMMAND... names the command, run with no shell in that run's workspace. AUTOCODE_CHANGESET_WORKSPACES holds a JSON object from each run's repository name to its workspace, so the consumer's tests can run against the producer's checkout. This is where the shared interface is checked. Naming a command clears both the previous result and its waiver, including when changing only the target.
  • changeset verify --run-dir RUN runs it. A check that changes a workspace does not pass.
  • changeset waive --run-dir RUN --reason TEXT records a waiver for the named check, current member runs and code. It grants no waiver for a replacement check.
  • changeset reopen --run-dir RUN --target TARGET [--message TEXT] sends that run a follow-up, by default the failed check's command and output.
  • changeset order --run-dir RUN TARGET... sets the merge order. By default the source run merges first.
  • changeset pr-body --run-dir RUN --target TARGET prints the Markdown section that run's pull request carries: the change set id, every run, the merge order, the check's outcome or the waiver, and the parts no run of the set covers.

docs.title: Change sets in clients
docs.text:
Each runs --json row carries changeset, the id of the change set its run belongs to, or null. A client (owner decision 2026-10-25) may read autocode changeset status --run-dir RUN --json for a run whose status view lists scope.linked, and take only the two argument arrays it names, after showing what they act on:

  • approval.next_command, after showing every run's plan. It carries the set_token of those plans, so a revision in any run makes the core refuse it.
  • verification.next_command, the joint check.

Approval displays include each plan's scope_exclusions under Not covered, including work left to another repository. The terminal, GitHub bridge, dashboard and VS Code show these terms before approval; a set approval shows them for every member. Recorded replay approval matching also includes exclusions and Git delivery, so changing only those terms still requires a new match.

The shared rule is autocode_client_actions.changeset_action, mirrored by vscode-extension/src/core/next-command.ts. The terminal chat's side panel lists the linked runs, /changeset shows the set and offers these actions, and /runs groups the chats of one change set. VS Code's Run details shows the set with one button for the action named now. The channel bridge posts the set's plans at a plan gate and takes approve set only with the set token of the plans it posted (docs/channels.md). The other changeset commands stay the person's own.

docs.title: Dependencies between existing runs
docs.text:
An already authorized delivery should not become a request for a person to assemble hashes and review logs. At an exact stopped permission request, an operator can bind the consumer to a producer using --bind-dependency SPEC.json (also TaskRun.bind_dependency). The specification names producer_workspace, producer_run, question_id, the current request_token, a human-readable label, an explicit files list, and a destination beneath the consumer run's evidence/. This action delegates only that delivery, records the authorization, and presents WAITING_FOR_DEPENDENCY / needs.kind=dependency, with no question to answer. It cannot consume a plan approval or artifact acceptance request.

Run python tools/autocode_dependencies.py --workspace CONSUMER --run-dir RUN --watch to supervise this binding. The worker uses TaskRun.status, never another run's private state. The additive view.delivery exists only for runner-verified current completion, with the source snapshot, approved contract and independently recorded Tester/completion review pins. The worker waits without model calls, copies only the declared regular files into an atomic evidence bundle, checks the producer again, then calls --receive-dependency MANIFEST and continues the consumer. It never imports source into the consumer itself or accepts the consumer's integration result.

Both the binding and delivered receipt survive restarts. A single worker lock prevents duplicate transports; a crash after publishing the bundle is safely replayable. Changed producer source, missing review pins, modified deliveries and changed consumer source/contracts block transport or resume. Operator feedback or an edited plan cancels the wait so the new decision can be reviewed. Keep the worker running while waiting; if it exits with an error, reconcile the reported cause and restart it against the same run. A failed/incomplete producer cannot release the consumer.

TaskRun.grant_recovery(N) explicitly grants a positive number of additional recoveries after the operator inspects saved work and fixes the cause. It preserves recovery history and uses the CLI checkpoint guards. resume_paused() and operational guidance do not grant an allowance.

docs.title: Failed workflow jobs
docs.text:
When a sessionless report_file bug Investigator lost its controller after writing a report but before the exit/result checkpoint, status() may expose job_report_recovery: the exact owned report path, its sha256, attempt_id, original source_identity, and a bound token. Read the report and inspect the attempt before calling run.recover_job_report(token) (CLI: --recover-job-report TOKEN). This is explicit adoption of those exact bytes, not a claim that the provider completed successfully. The raw exit remains unknown and stage history records operator recovery provenance. The action loads and applies the report normally, including the reproduction probe, and launches no model; continue separately afterwards.

The offer is read-only and disappears if the report, source capture, original source, configuration, or cleanup evidence is invalid or changed. All recorded workers and the independent keeper must be conclusively dead, with an authenticated owner-loss receipt proving cleanup. Timeouts, uncertain cleanup, rejected or malformed output, foreign/symlink paths, session/event reports, writers and report-repair attempts are not eligible. There is no durable provider report finalization seal, so presence/schema validity alone never authorizes automatic adoption. Plain attach/resume retains a valid offered attempt without applying or replaying it. No offer is inferred for an already archived job failure.

A stopped Reviewer, Architect, Analyst or Investigator publishes needs.kind = "retry_job", retaining its owning stage and archived transcript. Inspect needs.archive, needs.reason and needs.write_diagnosis; then call run.retry_job(view["needs"]["job_retry_token"]) for one fresh attempt under the saved source, route and limits. The CLI equivalent is --resume-paused --retry-failed-stage --job-retry-token TOKEN. A plain resume keeps the pause. Stale source/configuration, a token for a different attempt, or unresolved restoration is rejected before any model request.

A person can change only the total time/accounting caps of that exact stopped job with autocode --run-dir RUN --job-retry-token - --max-seconds SECONDS --max-cost-usd USD --no-chat (AUTOCODE_JOB_RETRY_TOKEN supplies the displayed token; either total flag may be omitted). This standalone settings action checks the original source and captured configuration before saving anything. It preserves usage and failed-attempt evidence, keeps the job paused and issues a fresh retry token; it grants no retry or plan approval. Read status again and explicitly retry with that fresh token. The old token, mixed actions, model/effort changes and other limits are refused. Clients may use this operator action only when offered by their public status contract; its availability as a CLI command does not authorize a client to invent a cap increase (#2156).

A job stopped by its provider's content filter, on quota, or by its stage time limit also carries needs.route (the shape of the answer need's route: question_id, role, job, current_model, engine, cause, stopped_model, and candidates for a refusal). The same model is likely to refuse again, so before retrying, a person can name another model: run.assign_model(role, model) answers --answer route-ROLE=MODEL --job-retry-token TOKEN with the view's token. The spec-first acceptance-test writer uses its own route-acceptance_tester question; an explicit answer changes only that saved writer route, leaving the later Tester (sol) and Completion Reviewer unchanged. A retained acceptance-writer timeout without a saved question is projected only from its matching archived timed-out attempt, source identity and launch configuration. This read changes no evidence and grants no retry authority. A model the launch would refuse, or the refused model itself, raises and changes nothing. An accepted model is saved as a route_assignment and the need comes back with a new job_retry_token; the old one is rejected. Its route is asked again against the new configuration: current_model is the named model, and candidates never lists it (answering it again is refused). Then call run.retry_job(view["needs"]["job_retry_token"]). assign_model updates every existing split or equals-form --ROLE-model in the client's options, so the retry never passes the old model back; the CLI refuses a --ROLE-model change for the stopped role at this stop (it would make the exact retry stale), unless it puts back the model the retry is bound to. The answer carries no other setting: given with a limit or another role's model it is refused and nothing is saved, and the CLI refuses it next to --resume-paused --retry-failed-stage (the retry needs the new token). After a refusal, output-limit or timeout stop, until a different model is named, the need's action is that answer (--answer route-ROLE=MODEL --job-retry-token TOKEN) and the recovery card offers no retry_job action for a refusal or output-limit stop, since the exact retry would replay the stopped model; the CLI still accepts the shown token. A quota stop keeps the retry in both, for once the quota resets. Once a model is named, progress.needs_you and the recovery card's what_happened ask only for the retry on it, and action and the card's retry_job carry that retry. The same holds when the job's uncertain attempt was set aside with --abandon-stage: the reason keeps the refusal or quota, the model and the provider's words. The Architect, Analyst and Investigator routes have no flag; only this answer moves them (an --investigator-model in the options pins the stuck-stage Investigator and is left as it is).

A missing or corrupt capture file does not prevent retry if the current source exactly matches the identity saved before the attempt, including file modes and Git HEAD. After manual restoration, the same token can be used; the old unrestored/write_diagnosis fields remain historical evidence and the CLI rechecks the full identity. It does not reconstruct an original identity from the current checkout.

In status schema 2, an older attempt that never recorded its original identity exposes needs.kind = "recover_source" and action = null, with recovery_hint. Its token, archive and diagnosis remain available for inspection, but cannot authorize an exact retry. Inspect the retained work and current changes before starting a new run. No automatic restart or budget reset occurs.

docs.title: Saved code checkpoints
docs.text:
status()["code_checkpoints"] adds immutable source receipts for recorded, code-changing Builder steps. A parallel batch's verified integration is one saved step: its milestone_id is null and members names each milestone it served with the files that milestone's Builder changed (members is null on other steps). Historical step metadata without source objects is inspectable but cannot be restored. recorded_check is historical, never current proof. This interface does not silently materialize snapshots for old runs.

Use compare_checkpoint(id) to inspect all changed paths and a bounded textual diff (including uncommitted additions). restore_checkpoint(id, expected_token, request_id) requires that exact comparison and returns a new TaskRun on a new managed branch. The original branch, staged changes, run and later work remain intact. Restoration is supported at an explicit reconciled pause of an ordinary build run with the same approved contract. Active workers/checks, pending interventions, human decisions, terminal Stop, progressive contracts and other workflow kinds refuse with an explanation; no worker is interrupted.

The new continuation is paused, with the exact plan approval, saved settings, model routes, limits and consumed allowances preserved. All milestones require fresh proof. Implementation/validation/completion and human artifact acceptance are not inherited as current. Earlier finding dispositions are restored; later open findings are marked rolled back, with complete original history retained in restoration-history.json and on the original run. Explicit resume_paused() uses the normal Builder/Validator/completion gates. No approval or provider call happens during restoration. Replaying the same request reconciles its owned candidate; changed or uncertain partial candidates are preserved and refused.

The CLI equivalent is autocode checkpoint --workspace WORKTREE --run-dir RUN --compare CHECKPOINT, followed by the mutually exclusive --restore CHECKPOINT --expected-token TOKEN --request-id ID. The dashboard uses this supported interface, places confirmation in chat and comparison in the Changes pane.

While a Builder step runs, code_checkpoints.working (otherwise null) names one more action in the same shape, autocode checkpoint --working. It is display only: it prints {since, changed_files, patch, truncated, compared_at}, the files as they are now against the newest saved step (since is its id) or, before any step is saved, against the checked-out commit (since is "start"), limited to the run's own scope. It carries no token and restores nothing. The Builder may still be writing, so a file changing during the read makes the action refuse; ask again.

Each row of code_checkpoints that still has verified source objects also names the actions a client may take, in the same shape as a connection (actions with id, label and next_command: an argument array following autocode). A client executes only offered actions. The compare action is always named on an available row. The restore action is named only where restoration is currently allowed (blocked_reason is null); it carries --expected-token -, which reads AUTOCODE_CHECKPOINT_EXPECTED_TOKEN and is supplied only by a fresh compare of that same checkpoint (a stale token is refused), and the REQUEST_ID placeholder, which the client replaces with its own stable id for this confirmation — replaying the same id reconciles its candidate instead of creating another. Without the run's paths the array uses the WORKSPACE and RUN_DIR placeholders; the status view supplies the real ones.

status()["changes_by_criterion"] attributes those saved steps to the approved plan's acceptance criteria. Each criterion lists the plan milestones that cover it, the checkpoint ids of their saved Builder steps and the union of the files those steps changed; a parallel batch's step counts only each member's own files toward that member's milestone. overlapping is true when a step outside the criterion's milestones also changed one of those files, so the file's diff may hold other work. unattributed lists steps whose milestone is not in the plan. It is attribution, not proof: it says where to look, not that the changes satisfy the criterion. It is null until a plan is approved.

status()["dev_server"] is the run's development server (Development server): configured says whether the run saved a serve command, status is off, starting, running, stopped, exited, failed or lost, and url is set only while it is running. code_checkpoint names the code checkpoint the server was started on and restarts counts the code changes that restarted it, and waiting is true while a server that exited or failed waits for the run's next code change to start again; a client can compare code_checkpoint with the latest code_checkpoints row to tell whether the preview shows the newest code. The status command inspects it on every call; a direct run_view.view() without that inspection leaves it null. Starting and stopping the server is autocode serve, not a TaskRun method, and it never changes the run.

docs.title: Conversation task provenance
docs.text:
New dashboard attachments, including saved legacy conversations, carry a canonical autocode.conversation-task envelope. The full validated handoff remains in the task presented to workers: human and assistant messages, titles, structured drafts, routes and receipts are retained. Only its human messages are requirement sources; assistant suggestions and unapproved drafts do not become mandatory requirements. Later human feedback and answers retain their existing source rules. A human can adopt a suggested literal by requesting it in a message, feedback or answer.

Source projection requires the complete canonical envelope and valid handoff digest. Extra instructions, altered envelopes and ordinary CLI tasks retain whole-task source semantics. Existing saved flattened tasks are not rewritten or reinterpreted. This format changes neither model routes nor the legacy/continuous handoff controls, and conveys no approval to implement.

docs.title: Current verification ownership
docs.text: status() includes additive verification_obligation metadata when a scheduled clean replay is pending. It names the current obligation separately from the saved runner_check, including its phase, exact preparation admission and current native command custody. runner_check_matches_current tells whether the saved check describes that same command. Status binds the current attempt, admission, phase/owner and command hierarchy before inspecting liveness, including genuinely live workers; it does not require a stopped result merely to display them. An admitted or post-execution phase with no current custody borrows no earlier command's liveness. A legacy unbound marker or unavailable ownership remains held; status does not reconcile it, grant a retry or establish test success. Use the displayed supported recovery action and retain interrupted receipts separately from fresh verification.

docs.title: Connections for clients
docs.text:
Connection setup is a core interface alongside task runs. A client may read autocode connections list --json before starting a task. The version-1 object contains connections, each with id, label, connection_status, detail, and actions. The connection new runs use without --provider (AUTOCODE_PROVIDER, then default_provider in ~/.config/autocode/config.toml, else opencode) also has default: true; it is display only, so a client can say what a new chat runs on. An action has id, label, and next_command: an argument array following autocode, not shell text. Clients execute only offered actions. Listing reads user-level provider configuration and executable availability; it never launches models, reads credential stores, or runs backend commands. The plain view carries routes: null and routes_next_command (["connections", "list", "--routes", "--json"]).

That named action adds the route each role would use, chosen from the connected tool's own model listing (#2057): tool, routes (each with role, job, model, tool, account, billing, reasoning_effort, origin), the same text as routes_lines, and routes_stop when no connected account can field a qualified route for a role. It reads a listing and never launches a model. A client shows routes_lines beside the connection; it does not choose a route itself.

connections check --provider NAME --json checks the backend without inference. Its result is one connection object. credentials_present means the backend reported credentials, not that every model, billing route or live task passed. Other statuses are not_checked, unavailable, sign_in_required, and check_failed. Status-command output and credential values are never returned.

connections login --provider NAME delegates interactive login to the backend in a terminal, inheriting its input and output. The core resolves the offered backend command again; the client supplies no credentials or executable. Login does not alter a task or start inference. After login the person checks again. A remote CLI wrapper must forward a terminal for interactive login (for example, a container transport needs a TTY). Connections are checked in the CLI's own execution environment, which may differ from the editor host.

Changing a client's selected backend applies to new chats. Existing task actions use their saved provider, models and budgets. Backend-specific role overrides must not be copied onto a different backend.

The always-present autocode connection advertises a setup action with next_command=["connections", "setup"]. Execute it interactively in a terminal, with no credential arguments or webview input. Its additional setup states are setup_required and configured; clients must not describe configured as authenticated live access. The core setup action neither chooses a client's default backend nor launches a model. Discovery reads its nonsecret metadata; an explicit check validates its private local credential setup. When several API providers are configured (issue #2055), the same row instead offers an add action with next_command=["connections", "add"], executed the same interactive way; it adds or rotates one provider's key without touching the others.

docs.title: Stage choices for clients
docs.text:
A client may let a person choose the model and reasoning level of each stage, as one dropdown per stage (Choosing each stage's model). autocode stages list --json [--backend NAME] returns the version-1 view: backend, label, file (where the choices are kept), options_stop (why no model could be listed, or null) and stages, in the order a task runs them. Each stage has id, label, does (what the stage does), advice (the kind of model and level that suits it), flag and effort_flag, default (model, effort, and offered: whether the backend offers that model), chosen (the saved model and effort, or null), options, set and reset. Each option has model, levels and levels_listed (whether the levels come from the tool's own listing), effort_choices (the levels a person may pick, or ["default"] for a model that lists none), family, context, account, billing and unavailable: the reason the stage may not run that model beside the others, or null.

A client shows label, does and advice, lists the options, and greys out an option whose unavailable is set, showing its reason. To save a choice it takes set.next_command, an argument array following autocode, replacing MODEL with one of options[].model and EFFORT with one of that option's effort_choices, and refuses anything else. reset.next_command (null until a choice is saved) forgets the stage's choice. Both print the updated view, and a refused choice exits 2 with the reason on stderr and saves nothing. The view launches no model and reads no credential. A new task reads the choices when it starts; a running task keeps its own.

docs.title: Run modes for clients
docs.text:
A client that starts runs may offer a choice of how much planning a new run does before the person approves it. autocode modes list --json returns the version-1 list: schema_version, default (a mode id) and modes, each with id, label, description and start_args, an argument array of start flags following the brief. A client shows the label and description and passes the chosen mode's start_args unchanged when it starts a run; it never builds its own list or adds flags to a mode. The flags apply only to the new run: a saved run keeps the flow it started with. Listing launches nothing and reads no run. Optional spend_confirmation is "planning" for Full mode: start the Requirements conversation without a spend dialog, then honor the core's review confirmation before preparing the plan. Requirements conversation still uses the selected model allowance. A mode with "start" (none today) can plan immediately, so a client confirms at launch. Missing or unknown metadata retains confirmation at launch for older cores.

Mode Start flags What it changes full (default) --joint-planning --spec-first Requirements talks with the person and confirms what it understood before the plan is prepared (Spec-first runs).

Every chat starts with the Requirements conversation (owner decision, 2026-10-22), so full is the only mode listed. The quick mode (--joint-planning --no-spec-first --adaptive-planning), which let a clear request skip Requirements, was removed; the --adaptive-planning flag itself remains. A client still reads the list rather than assuming one mode, and a choice it saved that the list no longer names, such as quick, starts the default instead of failing.

Every mode keeps the plan approval, the Tester and the Completion Reviewer: a mode changes how much planning happens before approval, never what counts as done. A CLI without modes (exit 2 with a usage error) offers no choice; a client then starts the full flow.

docs.title: Automatic routes for new runs
docs.text: New runs automatically select qualified models from the chosen tool's connected accounts, preferring subscriptions and preserving independent checking. No per-role model flags are needed, including with TaskRun.start(workspace, brief). Explicit model, effort and tool overrides win; saved runs keep their choices. --no-auto-select retains fixed defaults; conversation creation accepts both selection switches too. --auto-select requires selection to succeed instead of falling back when discovery or an independent checker is unavailable. See automatic model selection for discovery, reasoning levels, bounded preflight, recovery and the read-only selection preview.

docs.title: Repeated permission handoffs
docs.text:
PAUSED_PERMISSION_LOOP stops a fourth permission handoff after three authenticated material decisions at the same task, contract, source and validation result. Changed wording, report paths, elapsed time, budget settings and previous answers do not renew that allowance. This is a conservative bound on unchanged work, not a semantic claim that every question has identical wording or intent. Actual source, contract or validation progress admits new decisions; corrective --feedback can establish a new scope. No prior permission or completion gate is silently bypassed.

The public needs includes permission_decisions, permission_decision_limit, the saved blocker reason, and a named feedback action. Plain resume remains held without another provider call. All earlier requests, answers and usage remain retained.

docs.title: Authentication during an exact job retry
docs.text:
A retained workflow job that failed provider authentication offers the same token-bound model answer as other model-related job failures: inspect view.needs.route, call TaskRun.assign_model(role, model, job_retry_token=token), and then use the newly issued view.needs.job_retry_token with TaskRun.retry_job. The model answer launches nothing and preserves effort, other roles, limits and recorded usage. Alternatively, repair the existing provider login and retry that exact job unchanged.

If billing or authentication preflight blocks an authorized job retry before the job launches, the public view retains that exact job's retry and model-choice actions. It does not offer an ordinary Resume that would discard the job's retry boundary. An old token, consumed authorization, different next stage or active attempt cannot revive a previous failed job. No automatic provider substitution or credential copy is performed.

docs.title: Model choice after a stopped job timeout
docs.text:
A fully stopped workflow job that exceeded its stage limit can name another model through the same exact job-token answer. needs.route.cause is timeout; choosing a model changes only that job's model, rotates its retry token and launches nothing. It preserves other roles (including a bug Investigator's Plan Reviewer), effort, limits, usage and the archived attempt. A same-model exact retry is still accepted, but can time out again; no model or time-limit change is automatic.

When the stopped model declares a lighter reasoning variant than the one the job launched at (the tool's listing, or a level a preflight probe passed), the question offers that variant first (#1902): needs.route.lower_effort is {model, from, to, answer}, needs.route.candidates is [answer], and next_command is that answer, --answer route-ROLE=MODEL@LEVEL --job-retry-token -. This covers the deadline and the Investigator's exploration-budget stop alike. The answer form MODEL@LEVEL names the effort with the model; a level the model does not declare is refused and changes nothing, and with no listing the launch's own check decides. The named level is saved as the person's, bound into the rotated retry token, and the retry launches at it. A model without a lower declared variant gets the question as before.

A saved bug-Investigator timeout without a route question can expose one only when the archived rejected, timed-out attempt matches its source capture, launch route, configuration and archive. An active/uncertain attempt or a mismatch cannot gain that model action. The answer then rechecks source and configuration before it is saved, and the explicit retry checks the newly bound token.

docs.title: Explicit review intake and result freshness (#2113, #2167)
docs.text:
A new chat explicitly started with --workflow review goes directly to its Reviewer; it does not gather build requirements or request implementation-plan approval. Unpinned chat intake and build approvals are unchanged. Only the review's Validator route is due for model preflight; a saved unused Builder route is not probed. Probe receipts still bind to the exact tool, model and effort.

For completed reviews, view.evidence.workflow_result preserves the recorded outcome, summary, report path and digest. New reviews also record source_revision after the core writes its report. Status exposes a separate view.review_result inspection with freshness (current, stale_or_unverified, or unknown) and reasons after comparing that binding and report digest with the current workspace. Old reviews without a source binding remain unknown; status does not upgrade them or rerun a model. A review outcome is not build-delivery acceptance. The authenticated evidence.workflow_result stays unchanged by read-time inspection. The terminal renders these public review facts in its header, Review result panel and /details.

docs.title: Original-test command recovery
docs.text: At an idle validation pause, the core can name --resume-paused --revise-protected-tests @approved-suite when an approved empty package-marker deletion stranded the original root unittest collector for nested repositories. The needs.reason displays both exact commands and the retained original-test guarantee; clients take only that named action after confirmation. This revises only the suite command, capturing the same sealed original files from their archive, never the current modified tests. The old binding and explicit user event remain. The proposal starts from a unique approved, unfiltered pytest collector covering every original path. If restoring the sealed empty root marker would collide with an empty nested test package, the explicit offer moves the joint tests root first and adds --import-mode=importlib; it displays this exact change for confirmation and retains both markers. Executable nested package setup cannot trigger this correction. Active, uncertain, unapproved, filtered or ambiguous cases offer no correction. Fresh original-test replay and independent validation remain required.

docs.title: Single-host team service: contract proposal (#2023)
docs.text:
Status: proposed, not implemented or approved. Source audit: master 51728f73b031036f84d6575577596b53c9290df1, 2026-10-27. This document is the consolidated service/client-extension decision for #2022 and #2023. Merging this proposal does not authorize runtime implementation or expose a host. The synthetic envelopes are design fixtures, not service responses or qualification results.

The intended outcome is a verified pull request after a person submits work and disconnects. A durable worker is only one component of that outcome. Keep the existing core controller, TaskRun, supported Linux execution boundary, Requirements and exact-plan approval, separate Tester and Completion Reviewer, routes, efforts, usage, recovery and spending semantics. No automatic merge, deployment, Jira/Slack adapter, fleet or multi-team tenancy is proposed here.

docs.title: Decision package
docs.text:
The recommended first release uses one prepared persistent Linux host, one operator-owned repository registry, one OIDC login integration, a private service database and a thin authenticated web client. Notifications use the per-person service inbox and SMTP email as the single outbound channel. No action is accepted through email. These are proposed choices, not defaults silently enabled by this document.

The owner decision must cover the client extension, the permission/delegation rules below, the OIDC/session boundary, email notifications, the proposed trusted-actor core addition and the implementation scope #2024–#2032. The identity-provider instance, repositories, recipients, resource limits, routes and bounds are operator installation inputs; no real accounts or host settings are configured here. A separately agreed bounded pilot and thresholds remain

docs.title: 2033. No paid trial or production deployment is included in this package.
Responsibility and trust
docs.text:
Component Owns Cannot do Authentication / #2024 Validated principal, sessions, membership and permission revisions Trust request actor, Git identity or workspace configuration as login Service registry / #2026 Approved repository IDs, refs, setup/check profiles and credential references Accept arbitrary URLs, host paths or task-written policy Gateway / #2027 Authorize and translate opaque IDs to public TaskRun operations Import CLI/controller internals, read private task state or construct task policy Admission / #2028 Persist and schedule submissions, reconcile public launch receipts Become a second stage controller or replay an uncertain launch Execution boundary / #2025 Prepared task workspace, process/storage/secret isolation Treat a worktree or shared provider home as an isolation boundary Core Run lifecycle, locks, decisions, provider supervision, proof and completion Infer remote authentication from Git email or --as Web client / #2029 Render authorized projections and explicit human choices Receive raw core tokens, CLI argument arrays or host paths Inbox / #2030 Durable per-recipient attention and delivery notifications Approve, resume, retry or change limits on acknowledgement Publisher / #2031 Reconcile publication of an immutable verified result Publish arbitrary working HEAD, force-push or auto-merge Operations / #2032 Health, audit, backup/restore, drain and pinned upgrade records Delete uncertain attempts or manufacture recovered completion

Operator policy, service records and identity/publishing secrets live outside all agent-editable workspaces. Distinct execution identities and the supported kernel boundary prevent task processes from reading them. The service process and pinned core runtime are trusted; task code, generated reports, workspace Git/configuration and artifact HTML are untrusted. This is a trusted-team single-host boundary, not a hostile multi-tenant SaaS claim. Actual enforcement is a release gate in #2025, not established by this proposal.

docs.title: Authentication and authorization
docs.text:
Use an established OIDC library with authorization-code login and PKCE S256. Pin one configured issuer and client audience, exact redirect URI and signing algorithm policy; validate signatures, issuer, audience, expiry, state and nonce. Stable person identity is the (issuer, subject) pair, mapped to an operator-managed opaque principal_id; display name and email grant nothing. These protocol choices follow OIDC Core and OAuth security BCP, rather than a new password or token parser.

Terminate TLS at one configured reverse proxy on the prepared host. The gateway listens only on a private Unix socket, accepts forwarding metadata only from that proxy, and never consumes forwarded user/role headers as authentication. Use an opaque, server-side, revocable browser session with Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie, a configured short idle/absolute expiry and CSRF protection for every write. Do not put OIDC tokens in browser storage or task environments. No anonymous endpoints expose task/project inventory. Health without task data may be exposed only through operator configuration.

Permissions are deny-by-default and scoped to projects and, where needed, tasks. read does not imply submit; submit does not imply decide.

Operation Reader Submitter Designated decider Operator Inventory, status, approved artifacts Authorized project/task only Same Same Only with separate read grant Submit a new task No Granted project only Only with submit grant Only with submit grant Answer, feedback, approve exact displayed plan, named pause/recovery action No Only with explicit task decide grant Assigned task only No implicit task decision Acknowledge inbox Own inbox only Own inbox only Own inbox only Own inbox only Change registry, membership or drain service No No No Yes, audited Expand limits/routes or delegate protected choices No No implicit grant Only an explicitly presented, allowed core action and separate authority No bypass through service administration

The task owner receives read access through a recorded grant; permission to submit alone is not a reusable right to inspect someone else's task. Task ownership/decider changes require a recorded authorized operation, recheck the recipient's access and never transfer an already approved decision to a new plan. No owner-controlled arbitrary sharing is included in v1.

Check current membership, policy revision and task grant on every read, artifact fetch and decision application. Revocation invalidates sessions and future authority, including already queued human decisions and unsent email. It does not kill a worker or approve recovery. A revoked owner's running task becomes operator attention for reassignment through policy; the core retains its actual state. Filter list results and return the same not_found response for unknown and inaccessible object IDs. Audit the internal distinction.

docs.title: Repository and execution policy
docs.text:
A registry entry is operator-owned and immutable by version. A submission pins its project/repository ID, canonical remote identity, resolved base commit, registry version and execution-profile digest. An allowed base ref is resolved server-side once; changing its remote target later cannot silently rebase the submitted task. Revalidate access and current operator revocations at dispatch. A revoked policy blocks dispatch; it does not silently substitute a new one.

An entry contains:

  • Stable project/repository ID, canonical forge/repository identity, allowed base refs and service branch namespace. No request-supplied remote/path.
  • Toolchain/runtime image or prepared-host profile identity; reproducible setup and required checks as operator-reviewed argument arrays, working directory and allowed environment keys. Execute setup inside the task boundary.
  • Route/effort profile and existing core limits/policies; user-visible before acceptance. A named profile selects approved choices; the service cannot replace models or turn on compact planning to make a job pass.
  • Credential references separated into read-checkout, task-model and publisher capabilities. References resolve outside workspaces. No privileged service home, login/session store or publication token is copied to task processes.
  • Host/project/repository active-worker limits, queue/scratch/storage bounds, retention class, allowed task owners/deciders and publication destinations.
  • Accounting coverage policy: v1 preserves the core's accounting cap and explicit unknowns. Admission is blocked when an operator-required price or provider allowance is unavailable; it never calls an estimate a guaranteed bill. Monthly/person quotas or new strict spending guarantees are not added.

Before model work, validate repository/ref/credential access, supported durable mode, containment, setup and check availability. Setup that runs untrusted repository code must already be isolated. Separate invalid submissions from a later unavailable prerequisite. No quiet downgrade to owned execution, another engine or weaker isolation. Same-repository tasks use distinct workspace/branch identities plus existing checkout locks. Multi-repository coordination is not silently enabled: current durable anchors refuse automatic coordination, so v1 rejects unsupported spanning scope rather than delivering a partial result.

docs.title: Public v1 envelopes
docs.text:
Use /api/v1 and JSON with a version discriminator. Reject unknown request fields, invalid types and unsupported versions. IDs are opaque service IDs; clients never send or receive run directories, core control tokens, shell strings, CLI arrays or credential references. Server-only mappings bind each ID to the allowed public core handle. Text is untrusted data; preserve its multiline/Unicode content within documented size limits.

Route / envelope Required request fields Response and authority POST /tasks / submission version, project/repository IDs, allowed base_ref, requirements, acceptance criteria, execution_profile_id, explicit delegation record Durable admission receipt, task ID, payload digest, resolved base/policy identities; no execution promise GET /tasks / inventory Authorized filters and opaque cursor Only visible tasks; no hidden repository counts or IDs GET /tasks/{id} / status Opaque task ID Independent admission/execution/delivery state, observation freshness, accounting coverage, permitted artifacts and current decision offer POST /tasks/{id}/decisions / decision version, opaque decision_id, exact observed revision, explicit offered choice and typed payload Durable decision receipt; applied, refused or pending/unknown. Never immediate claimed completion GET /tasks/{id}/decisions/{receipt} Receipt ID Durable action outcome or explicit unresolved reconciliation GET /tasks/{id}/artifacts/{id} Opaque authorized artifact ID Allowlisted bounded inert content, digest/type/size; no arbitrary path/open redirect GET /inbox, POST /inbox/{id}/acknowledge Recipient session; explicit read acknowledgement Local unread state only; no task action delivery in status No caller-supplied repository/commit/PR URL Verified result identity plus prepared/publishing/published/blocked/unknown state and reconciled PR URL

All writes carry an Idempotency-Key in a bounded documented format. Store the canonical validated request and its digest transactionally before returning 202 accepted; do not acknowledge a memory-only queue item. Scope uniqueness to principal + operation + object + key. The same request returns its original receipt. A different request under the same key returns 409 idempotency_conflict. Uniqueness is per key, not semantic deduplication of two intentionally new tasks. Retain tombstones for at least the task/decision retention period; an expired key cannot create a second task through a retry. Database failover/restore must preserve that boundary or hold admission pending operator reconciliation.

Canonical payloads use validated typed fields, sorted object keys and UTF-8 JSON with no insignificant whitespace, preserving array order and exact text without Unicode normalization. Use integer bounds or decimal strings, never non-finite numbers. Reject duplicate JSON keys before canonicalization. The service pins a canonicalization version with the receipt; an upgrade cannot reinterpret an old idempotency key.

Error codes: unauthenticated, not_found, invalid_submission, unsupported_version, idempotency_conflict, stale_decision, permission_revoked, policy_unavailable, capacity_unavailable, observation_unavailable, core_refused, and outcome_unknown. Return a correlation ID and retry guidance, with no secret/core token or host path. An HTTP error or timeout is never authority to repeat a provider operation.

docs.title: Current core capabilities and additive gaps
docs.text:
Service operation Current public capability Required boundary / gap owner New durable submission modes list --json, TaskRun.start_durable, inspect_launch #2028 persists server-owned binding and reconciles one launch Read current execution/proof TaskRun.status(inspect_evidence=True), evidence_report(require_current=True) #2027 filters/redacts the projection; unavailable is not a failed task Continue or answer a gate Fresh named action via shared NamedCommand and TaskRun.dispatch_durable #2024/#2027 add trusted actor/assertion receipt support before person actions ship Show the actual plan TaskRun.show_goal, current displayed-plan token and public view Gateway stores private token and exact rendered bytes, exposing only its own decision ID Current code diff Status code_checkpoints named comparison #2027 executes only that capability; no arbitrary Git/path RPC Per-person service inbox Public attention identity plus service-owned recipient/read records #2030 must not repurpose core same-UID attention acknowledgement as remote per-person state Read arbitrary artifact No universal authenticated download operation is established #2027 adds a public bounded capability for each supported kind, otherwise refuses it Verified general-task PR Existing issue/coordination delivery, not a universal TaskRun publisher #2031 adds/reuses a public named capability and immutable receipt; no private-state workaround Remote actor / lost decision outcome No verified service actor or assertion-id lookup is established #2024/#2027 additive core contract below; local Git provenance cannot fill this gap

The table is an audited distinction between existing methods and proposed capabilities. It is not a list of features already implemented by the service.

docs.title: Human decisions and attributable core actions
docs.text:
Before offering a decision, the gateway reads fresh public status, verifies its task binding and named action, and saves a private observation record. Its opaque decision_id binds task incarnation/turn, action kind, exact rendered plan/question bytes and digest, core checkpoint/token, policy revision and expiry. Only the human-readable content and service ID leave the host. A plan approval is a separate explicit choice against that exact displayed plan; fetching it, free text, a notification click or a previous approval is not consent.

At application, reauthenticate/re-authorize, re-read current status and compare all bindings. A changed plan/action or revoked grant refuses the decision and requires a new display. Pass only the fresh status-named argument array through the existing shared client-action machinery and durable transport. The core still checks its own token under its lock. Two people acting on the same gate cannot authorize two different actions: serialize application per bound gate; one receipt wins and the other is stale/refused. Never reuse the winner's receipt as the other person's approval.

Confirmed core gap: autocode_approval_provenance and autocode_required_approver explicitly record unverified Git/--as claims. They are not a remote authentication boundary. The current GitHub bridge allowlist and service-side authorization cannot turn those claims into verified core actor provenance. Do not set Git email or --as to impersonate a user.

Proposed additive capability, owned by #2024/#2027 before remote decisions ship:

  1. An operator-configured trusted service issuer attests the validated principal, authorization revision and receipt ID for one exact core decision binding. The binding includes run incarnation/turn, current action/checkpoint/token digest, rendered-content digest, decision payload digest, expiry and a unique single-use assertion ID. The authenticated actor is never supplied by the task workspace or remote request body.
  2. Use an established JWS implementation with pinned Ed25519 keys and EdDSA, following RFC 8037, and a pinned issuer/key policy outside agent-editable storage; no custom cryptographic parser. The signing key stays with the service, outside provider access. Transport the assertion privately alongside the exact named action, never as model context, public argv, an artifact or a new arbitrary CLI command. The precise TaskRun transport/descriptor is part of that additive implementation review.
  3. The core verifies the assertion, exact current binding, trusted issuer and allowed service policy under its decision lock before mutation. Consume its assertion identity atomically with the decision event and expose an additive authenticated_actor/service-receipt audit projection. An unknown outcome must be queryable by assertion/receipt identity without replaying the action.
  4. Existing local Git provenance remains explicitly unverified. No configured trust means the new assertion is refused, never treated as a local approval. Service-authorized subject grants must be separate from require-approver's local Git-email guard; a task cannot remove a trusted service guard by editing project configuration. Existing local behavior is preserved.

Until this addition exists and is qualified, the gateway must refuse remote person decisions. It must not claim #2024/#2027 complete using only an HTTP audit row. Contract and fixture work can proceed meanwhile. Core status, artifacts and lifecycle remain public interfaces; no private task-state access is added.

Upfront delegation is explicit, never inferred from requirements. The default submission records {"mode":"none"}. A separately authorized submitter may select {"mode":"core_policy","profile_id":...,"accepted_digest":...} for an operator-approved existing core recovery-policy profile. The service must display its exact existing flags, authority, maximums, financial guard and non-delegable decisions before recording that authenticated grant. It passes only that pinned new-run policy to TaskRun; it does not implement recovery or increase authority later. For example, an explicitly selected profile may use the existing --autoresolver-managed-limits semantics, including its existing ceilings and explicit-cap/unknown-usage exclusions. It cannot substitute routes, remove a financial cap, waive evidence or authorize an uncertain provider replay. The selected profile is installation policy, not authorized by this proposal.

Requirements confirmation, approval of an exact new plan, scope/permission changes, unsupported-effort choices and any core person-only recovery remain human gates. The notification names the designated decider. No blanket preapproval of future plans, skip-to-build or invented answers is introduced. A policy stop with no current named action remains held. Qualify both the no-delegation path and an explicit existing-policy grant without treating them as equivalent authority. Any broader company delegation is a separate decision.

docs.title: Admission, execution and delivery are separate
docs.text:
A task projection keeps these axes instead of using one misleading success:

  • Admission: accepted, queued, preparing, dispatching, dispatched, blocked, rejected. A committed receipt proves admission, not a launch.
  • Execution: not_started, running, waiting_for_person, paused, blocked, failed, core_complete, unknown. Public observation includes observed_at, available, current, core runtime and incarnation identity. A stale/unavailable observation never erases the last result or offers actions.
  • Delivery: not_ready, prepared, publishing, published, blocked, unknown. Core completion is not PR publication. Current completion receipt, exact verified commit/tree, approved destination and publication identity bind delivery. Later follow-up work has a new turn/result identity.

Dispatch commits a unique intent before TaskRun.start_durable; reconcile its public launch receipt with inspect_launch. Losing the start reply does not prove no worker exists. Do not call start again until public reconciliation establishes the outcome or an explicit supported recovery decision authorizes it. Queue fairness is bounded round-robin across projects and FIFO within a project, subject to registry/host limits and core checkout exclusion. Held work releases queue scheduling slots only when the actual worker state supports it; no scheduling policy grants a task resume or abort.

Publication intent binds service task/result, destination and exact verified commit before a remote side effect. Reconcile by branch/commit/PR identity after a lost response. Changed working HEAD must not replace the immutable verified result. A newer submitted base policy, stale evidence or unexpected remote branch blocks publication; never force-push to resolve it. Existing issue and coordination publication machinery is reused where its public capability fits. Missing general-task publication/evidence retrieval must be added as named public capabilities; #2031 cannot inspect issue-private files or invent CLI commands.

Accounting projects the public usage, cost and efficiency records with coverage, pricing basis, failed attempts and unknown stages. Preserve queue, provider-active, observed running-wall, human-wait and repair-wait categories; missing time is unknown. Use existing cost definitions. Subscription/API-equivalent estimates are not invoices, and stage-boundary caps are not guaranteed bills. #1867's broader policy remains unchanged.

docs.title: Inbox, artifacts and operations
docs.text:
Each logical notification binds recipient, task incarnation/turn and public attention/delivery identity. Persist unread state and an outbound outbox outside workspaces. Recheck current ownership/access before send or display; suppress superseded attention. Use the operator-configured SMTP relay and recipient mapping, with no destinations from task text. Email carries a generic state and an authenticated task link, not source, secrets, decision tokens or action links. A delivery timeout is unknown, not proof email was unsent; durable retry policy must preserve one logical notification and acknowledge possible duplicate mail. Inbox acknowledgement changes only the service recipient record, not core local attention receipts or task authority.

Artifacts are public-capability IDs resolved and authorized server-side. No raw filesystem browsing, symlink following or arbitrary HTML execution. Logs are bounded/redacted; treat Markdown/HTML/SVG as untrusted inert content with an appropriate download/content policy. A URL possession never substitutes for current access. If no public artifact capability exists, return unavailable and add the core capability before exposing that artifact.

Audit append-only service events for admission, authorization/revocation, decision intent/outcome, dispatch intent/reconciliation, notification and publication identities. Include the authenticated principal and policy revision; exclude secrets and core tokens. The service's audit receipt is correlated to, not substituted for, the core's actual event/evidence. Drain stops new dispatch, not running workers. Pinned-runtime upgrades cannot adopt uncertain attempts. Back up service records and supported core recovery artifacts consistently; restore holds dispatch until launch/publication ownership is reconciled. Cleanup requires current no-worker ownership and retention policy; uncertainty retains data. #2032 supplies and qualifies the actual runbooks and mechanisms.

docs.title: Shared qualification fixtures
docs.text:
Use two deliberately small independent repositories under test-only IDs: repo-pager (Python unittest paging CLI) and repo-totals (Python pytest aggregation function). Pin their seed commits, setup profiles, external oracles and broken variants in #2026; avoid installations by using prepared environments. These are proposed fixtures, not the historical live runs or an authorization to spend on two new tasks. #2033 agrees any live sample separately.

The synthetic v1 envelopes name person-a, person-b, these repositories and stable service IDs. They contain no real identity, credential or host path. The matrix below is required behavior for the dependent implementations; none is marked tested by this document.

Case Required observation / negative control Owner Two people, two projects A reads/submits/decides pager; B totals; swapped task/artifact/receipt IDs disclose nothing #2024/#2027 Same repository concurrency Distinct branches/workspaces, bounded scheduling and existing checkout locks; cross-task writes denied #2025/#2028 Duplicate admission and lost acknowledgement Same principal/key/payload returns one task; changed payload conflicts; death before commit has no accepted receipt #2028 Auth forgery Actor/header/Git-email/workspace edits, wrong issuer/audience/nonce, expired session and CSRF never authorize #2024 Revoked access Revoke after display, before apply/send; no mutation, artifact read or email; worker not silently killed #2024/#2030 Conflicting decisions A/B hold one gate; one applies, the other's receipt is refused/stale; no second model dispatch #2027 Stale plan or turn Revised plan/follow-up invalidates the old display; no automatic reapproval #2027/#2029 Lost decision receipt Reconnect queries the durable receipt/assertion identity; no second invocation from timeout alone #2027/#2028 Lost launch reply / service death Inspect the committed launch identity, retain unknown ownership and never blindly start again #2028/#2032 Blocked task / unavailable status Separate actual blocked state from unavailable observation; no speculative Resume or fabricated current completion #2027/#2029 Browser close and protected question Durable worker continues; inbox/email persists; authenticated fresh exact decision resumes only that gate #2029/#2030 Unknown pricing / in-flight cost Subtotal and coverage remain explicit; operator-required coverage blocks admission; no guaranteed bill claim #2028/#2033 Missing setup/isolation Preflight refusal before provider launch; no fallback to shared home or owned mode #2025/#2026 False green product Unrelated successful command and broken variant cannot satisfy approved criteria or delivery #2026/#2031 Moved HEAD / lost PR reply Publish only immutable verified commit or block; reconcile one known PR, no overwrite/force-push #2031 Artifact/notification attack Other-task IDs, path/symlink escape, active HTML and task-specified email cannot leak or advance work #2024/#2027/#2030 Reboot / restore / upgrade Every accepted receipt accounted for; interrupted/unknown provider work uses core recovery; no fabricated replay #2032

Component tests precede real supported-Linux containment/HTTP/browser/fault integration. Existing lifecycle evidence at its pinned revisions is reused but is not a service pass. Final pilot gates include the #2022 vague-brief evidence gap, a same-task follow-up, exact-commit independent acceptance and agreed cost, time and human-intervention thresholds. No threshold is invented here.

docs.title: Implementation order and open decisions
docs.text: After owner acceptance of this package, #2024 and #2027 implement identity and the additive core actor boundary; #2025/#2026 establish isolated repository fixtures; #2028 implements durable admission against those interfaces. #2029,

docs.title: 2030, #2031 and #2032 may develop against the shared envelopes concurrently,
docs.text:
